Title: 'Cottage hospitals' could be a game-changer for rural Malaysia
Article:
FEW healthcare ideas have the potential to deliver such immediate benefits to underserved communities as the Health Ministry's  proposed cottage hospital initiative.
At first glance, the concept appears straightforward. Selected rural health clinics will be upgraded with observation wards and enhanced medical capabilities, allowing patients to receive a broader range of treatments closer to home.
Yet behind this modest proposal lies a potentially transformative shift in how healthcare is delivered to some of Malaysia's most geographically isolated communities.
In his winding-up speech during the debate on the Supply Bill 2027 in the Dewan Rakyat recently, Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said the Health Ministry has identified four existing health clinics under the concept: Sungai Asap in Sarawak; Telupid and Nabawan in Sabah; and Tekek on Pulau Tioman, Pahang.
Their selection is no accident. Sungai Asap is  about 184km from Bintulu, while Telupid sits some 125km from Sandakan.
Nabawan, meanwhile, serves communities deep in Sabah's interior, far from Keningau, the nearest urban centre with more comprehensive medical facilities.
Together, they exemplify the geographical challenges that many rural Malaysians face in accessing healthcare.
The objective is clear: improve access to inpatient care, reduce the need for long-distance travel and ease congestion at larger hospitals.
These facilities are intended to serve as a bridge between ordinary health clinics and major referral hospitals, bringing healthcare closer to the people who need it most.
While each location has its own unique characteristics, they share a common challenge. Distance.
Nowhere is this challenge more evident than in Sarawak, whose immense land area, dispersed population and vast network of rural settlements mean that healthcare accessibility remains a constant concern.
Sungai Asap was established in the late 1990s as the resettlement area for communities displaced by the Bakun Dam, including many Orang Ulu families from the Sungai Balui basin.
Today, despite the area's development, residents of Sungai Asap and other interior settlements still face long journeys to major hospitals.
Such trips can be physically demanding, time-consuming and costly, particularly for the elderly, patients requiring regular monitoring and lower-income families.
The situation is equally relevant in Sabah.
Communities served by clinics in Telupid and Nabawan frequently live significant distances from specialist medical facilities.
Rural residents sometimes have little choice but to spend hours on the road to obtain treatment that could potentially be delivered closer to home if enhanced facilities were available locally.
For patients and caregivers alike, reducing travel time can greatly improve quality of life.
Pulau Tioman presents another compelling case. Islanders contend with geographical constraints that mainland residents rarely experience.
Accessing advanced medical care often means travelling by sea and then continuing onward to larger healthcare centres.
Weather conditions and transportation arrangements can further complicate matters.
Viewed collectively, these locations illustrate why the initiative deserves serious consideration. The Health Ministry is not simply upgrading buildings.
It is reimagining healthcare delivery in places where geography remains one of the greatest barriers to timely treatment.
The proposal is also notable because it emphasises the intelligent use of existing infrastructure.
Rather than embarking solely on costly new hospital construction projects, the government is exploring ways to strengthen facilities that are already embedded within communities.
This approach could shorten implementation timelines while delivering meaningful improvements in patient care.
Equally important is the potential impact on overcrowded hospitals.
Patients requiring observation, follow-up treatment or less complex inpatient care may no longer need to travel to major hospitals unnecessarily.
This would allow larger institutions to focus on highly specialised procedures and critical cases.
Success here will ultimately depend on execution. Adequate staffing, appropriate equipment, continuous training and sustainable funding will remain essential.
Rural communities deserve not only buildings, but also quality services delivered consistently and professionally.
Nonetheless, the underlying principle is both practical and compassionate. Communities should not face unnecessary disadvantages simply because of where they live.
If successful, the cottage hospital initiative under the Madani Reform Agenda championed by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim could emerge as one of the country's most meaningful healthcare reforms.
It reflects a simple but powerful belief: quality healthcare should reach the people, wherever they may live.
* The writer is a former Bernama chief executive officer and editor-in-chief

Title: Chen probe upends Shanghai route to the top
Article:
THE unexpected corruption investigation into Shanghai party chief Chen Jining, once seen as a strong contender for China's highest leadership body, challenges assumptions long used by diplomats and analysts to anticipate Beijing's opaque power moves.
Experts said the Shanghai party secretary post, a position once held by both President Xi Jinping and former president Jiang Zemin, was a well-trodden route to the party's top leadership posts that now appeared much less predictable.
"There is no more straight-forward pathway from Shanghai party secretary to the Politburo Standing Committee," said Wen-Ti Sung, a nonresident fellow at the Atlantic Council's Global China Hub, adding that political loyalty was the main criterion.
The sudden announcement of the investigation into Chen, an Imperial College London graduate in environmental engineering who stood out among his peers for having spent roughly a decade in Britain, surprised both the diplomatic and business communities.
Over nearly four decades, eight former Shanghai party chiefs were promoted to the Politburo Standing Committee. Chen's predecessor Li Qiang is now premier and sits on the current committee.
Chen, 62, was seen as a strong contender for elevation to the committee in the party's leadership reshuffle during the 21st Party Congress next year.
Xi is "clearing the ground" before the congress, sweeping aside entrenched political customs and older networks to build a more ideologically aligned leadership lineup, a senior Asian diplomat said.
China's anti-graft watchdog announced on Tuesday that Chen was under investigation for "suspected serious violations of discipline and law", a euphemism commonly used for corruption in China.
He had an unusual rise through China's official ranks. An environmental scientist by training, he rose through ​China's elite Tsinghua University, Xi's alma mater, to become its president.
He entered the government as China's environmental protection minister in 2015 — just as Xi made the area a priority — before becoming mayor of Beijing. He joined the Politburo in 2022 and was named party boss of Shanghai, China's financial hub.
A champion for artificial intelligence development in Shanghai and Beijing, Chen was last seen in public last week holding separate meetings with Chinese shipping company COSCO and the chairman of Swiss pharmaceutical firm Roche.
The brief turnaround between Chen's last public appearance and the probe is unusual. Senior party officials usually disappear from public view for extended stretches before an investigation is officially announced.
Xi's dismantling of reform-era term limit norms and promotion of loyalists, together with the high-pressure anti-graft drive, have disrupted established routes to elevation and succession.
In 2017, Sun Zhengcai, a former Chongqing party chief and Politburo member, who was viewed as a potential future leader, was abruptly removed and later sentenced to life in prison for corruption.
Chen is the fourth Politburo member investigated in just over a year as Xi's anti-corruption purge reaches the party's innermost circle, having already ensnared Central Military Commission vice-chairmen Zhang Youxia and He Weidong, as well as former Xinjiang party chief Ma Xingrui.
"Chen's purge is particularly shocking in that he poses no military threat, and doesn't deviate from Xi on major symbolic issues like ethnic policy," Sung said.
"But he got purged anyway, so far without even an explanation. The shock is bound to reverberate."
The writer is from Reuters

Title: Trump urges Putin to end 'military aggression' in Europe
Article:
WEST PALM BEACH: US President Donald Trump said Thursday he had asked Vladimir Putin to "pull back all military aggression" against Europe, in a fresh shift in tone towards the Russian leader he called his friend just last week.
Trump said he had made the request to Putin when they met in China last week, adding that he thought it would help lead to a deal to end Moscow's grinding war in Ukraine.
Trump's comments come a day after he hosted NATO chief Mark Rutte in Florida, after which the two leaders issued a joint statement calling on Russia not to expand the Ukraine war.
"During my conversations in China with President Vladimir Putin, of Russia, I spent a lot of time talking about the fact that I would like to see President Putin pull back all Military aggression against territories throughout Europe,"Trump said on his Truth Social network.
Trump said he had done so "in the hopes that a Deal can be made between Russia and Ukraine, and made quickly."
"I really believe this is a strong possibility – Thousands of people are being killed each and every month, A COMPLETE BLOODBATH – and will be a Great Tribute to everyone!"
The statement did not specify which territories Trump meant – and did not specifically include Ukraine, which Russia invaded in February 2022, kicking off the largest war in Europe since World War II.
But European nations have been increasingly concerned by what they regard as Russian provocations, including three Russian cruise missiles landing in Poland last week.
In their joint statement on Wednesday, Trump and NATO's Rutte said they "discussed the importance of Russia avoiding any actions that intentionally, or unintentionally, expand the war."
Trump, who is spending the US Thanksgiving holiday at his Mar-a-Lago resort, reposted the joint statement with Rutte on Truth Social shortly before his new comments on Putin.
In a notable contrast with Trump's recent criticisms of Ukraine for striking targets deep inside Russia, the US leader made no call for Kyiv to show similar restraint.
'DEADLOCK'
Trump's tone appeared markedly different to when Trump met Putin in the Chinese city of Shenzhen last week, both face-to-face and together with Chinese President Xi Jinping.
On that occasion, a smiling Trump welcomed Putin by saying "Who is he? He's my friend," before warmly shaking hands with the Russian leader.
The "friend" comment in particular renewed concerns in Kyiv and European capitals that Trump was once again pivoting towards the Russian leader he has long been close to.
Trump has often appeared more willing to blame Ukraine for Russia's invasion, and has had tense relations with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky since their televised blow-up in the Oval Office in February 2025.
The US envoys on the Ukraine war, Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner and business friend Steve Witkoff, have been accused of a similar willingness to take Moscow's side.
In an interview with the German MD Meets Podcast on Wednesday, Kushner said that Putin had "showed restraint" because he had "agreed not to use nuclear weapons."
Kushner also described the Russian leader, whom he has met several times, as a "grandmaster of politics" – while calling the Ukraine conflict "a proxy war where Europe is funding and arming Ukraine against Russia."
But he acknowledged that the issue of territory in eastern Ukraine claimed by Moscow remained a sticking point with Putin.
"What Steve and I have deciphered from having many, many hours with President Putin and from the Russian team, is that you know the territorial issue is right now a little bit of a deadlock," he said.
And he warned against any downward spiral in the Ukraine war, saying it "it won't take a lot of miscalculation for this thing to escalate massively."

Title: NST Leader: Keeping online scammers at bay
Article:
HERE'S why many Malaysians lose their shirts to online scammers: they are lulled in, not because they are gullible — though some are — but because modern scams are skilfully engineered to exploit human foibles.
Scammers have found a sweet spot  in exploiting trust and fear,  routinely using online digital technology to deceive victims.
Take the case of the Johor woman who saw a RM10 maid-booking service as nothing more than a sweet deal — only to find more than RM15,000 surreptitiously drained from her bank account after several  attempts to register.
Of course, the RM10 offer on social media was a tantalising bait. Scammers know the bait won't get any bite except from the naive.
Once they manipulated the  woman into providing her private banking details, they  transferred out her savings to temporary offshore accounts and   disappeared for good.
Online fraud has cost Malaysians RM7.33 billion since 2023.    About 192,869 complaints were filed until October this year.
While tracking these dastardly schemers is almost impossible, the authorities have made some headway. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail revealed that 75,266 people were arrested during the same period while 69,665 charges were brought against people linked to 137,699 mule accounts.
Let's get something clear: online transactions and banking are generally safe, provided users exercise care and follow security rules.
But no secure website or transaction can protect a user who carelessly enters banking credentials into a WhatsApp link.
Web security is useless if users install APK files or apps  pushed by online sellers.
Banking security collapses the moment  users  hand over one-time password,  transaction authorisation code  or banking approval codes.
These are basic precautions, yet most scam victims have, in one way or another, overlooked what is a powerful security  force field.
To stay safe, users must check and recheck bank accounts and cellphone numbers  through the government's Semak Mule portal as  a second line of defence.
Verify any  "attractive" online services and offers  and do not rely on  social media sales pitch.
If money is suddenly siphoned, immediately call the National Scam Response Centre at 997 and alert the relevant bank to freeze access.    Finally, lodge a police report.   Truth be told,  the person on a video call   with you may be computer-generated, even if they look and  sound like a best friend or close relative.
Scammers are even brazen enough to  impersonate officers from the police, Bank Negara Malaysia, Inland Revenue Board, High Court or government agencies.
These days, most  deal with these slick  scammers by  ignoring them or having the intuition to spot the deception.    Building experience, education and street savviness to install a mental scam detector may be the strongest psychological defence against ruthless online fraud.

Title: Abdul Gani Patail: Prosecutor behind Malaysia's high-profile cases
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Throughout his more than three decades in the legal profession, former attorney general Tan Sri Abdul Gani Patail played a pivotal role in several high-profile cases that captured public attention, establishing himself as a prominent figure in Malaysia's legal landscape.
Among the high-profile prosecutions Abdul Gani handled were the corruption case involving former Sabah chief minister Datuk Joseph Pairin Kitingan in 1993 and the case involving the Al-Ma'unah militant group in 2000.
The Lahad Datu-born legal figure also led the prosecution team in the case involving 30 individuals, including Philippine nationals, charged with waging war against the Yang di-Pertuan Agong and involvement in various terrorism-related activities in Lahad Datu, Sabah, in 2013.
Abdul Gani, who served as Attorney General for 13 years from 2002 to 2015, died at a private hospital here tonight due to an infection.
Attorney General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar, who confirmed the news of his death, also extended his condolences to Abdul Gani's family.
"The entire Attorney General's Chambers (AGC) extends its condolences to his family and prays that Allah showers His blessings upon his soul," Mohd Dusuki said when contacted.
Abdul Gani was also part of the prosecution team in the 2006 murder case involving Mongolian national Altantuya Shaariibuu.
He also led the prosecution of former Transport Minister Tun Dr Ling Liong Sik, who was charged in 2010 with cheating the Malaysian government in connection with the Port Klang Free Zone (PKFZ) scandal involving the RM1.08 billion purchase of land in Pulau Indah.
Abdul Gani also handled the prosecution of former Selangor Menteri Besar Dr Mohamad Khir Toyo on corruption charges relating to a property purchase.
He also led the prosecution team in the criminal breach of trust case involving RM76.4 million against former Perwaja Rolling Mill and Development Sdn Bhd managing director Tan Sri Eric Chia Eng Hock and handled the corruption case involving former Land and Cooperative Development Minister Tan Sri Kasitah Gaddam.
Born on Oct 6, 1955, Abdul Gani began his career in the Judicial and Legal Service in 1980 before serving as a deputy public prosecutor at the Attorney General's Chambers in Tawau, Sabah, becoming the first Sabahan to hold the position following the establishment of the federal Attorney General's office in the state.
Throughout his career, he held several key positions, including Sabah head of prosecution in 1991, head of the AGC's Prosecution Division from Jan 16 to Oct 14, 1994, and head and adviser of its International Affairs Division from April 1, 1995, to May 31, 1997.
He subsequently served as Commissioner of Law Revision from 1997 to 2000 before returning as head of the Prosecution Division on Feb 1, 2000.
On Nov 19, 2001, Abdul Gani was appointed Malaysia's eighth Attorney General and officially assumed office on Jan 1, 2002, making history as the first locally trained law graduate to be appointed to the position and the first Sabahan to hold one of the highest posts in the federal civil service.
The appointment marked a major milestone in his legal career, which saw him helm the country's foremost legal institution for more than 13 years before his tenure as Attorney General was terminated on health grounds, effective July 27, 2015.
However, he continued serving as an officer in the Judicial and Legal Service until reaching the mandatory retirement age on Oct 6, 2015.
Abdul Gani also contributed his legal expertise and experience through various other roles, including as a member of the Pardons Board for the Federal Territories of Kuala Lumpur, Labuan and Putrajaya.
He was also appointed an adjunct professor at the Faculty of Law of Universiti Teknologi MARA (UiTM) for two years from Oct 1, 2011, and served as chairman of the National Legal Aid Foundation (YBGK).
On Dec 23, 2016, he was admitted as an advocate and solicitor of the High Court of Malaya. -- BERNAMA

Title: SPM candidate fractures left leg in accident en route to exam
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A student who was on his way to sit for the Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) examination fractured his left leg after the motorcycle he was riding collided with a car in Jalan Bangsar Utama 1 this morning.
The accident occurred around 6.55am as the student was travelling from Pantai Dalam towards SMK Bangsar.
Kuala Lumpur Traffic Enforcement and Investigation Department chief Assistant Commissioner Suffian Abdullah said preliminary investigations found that the car, driven by a 25-year-old woman travelling in the opposite direction, was believed to have turned right without giving way to the motorcycle.
"This caused a collision between the two vehicles.
"The motorcyclist suffered a fracture to his left leg and was taken to Kuala Lumpur Hospital for further treatment, while the car driver was uninjured," he said in a statement.
Suffian said the case was being investigated under Section 43(1) of the Road Transport Act.
Anyone who witnessed the accident or has information is urged to contact the Tun H.S. Lee Traffic police station at 03-2071 9999 or any nearby police station to assist investigations.

Title: MoH to take action over video of rats eating bean sprouts at Pudu Market
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Health Ministry will coordinate an integrated enforcement operation with relevant agencies following a viral video showing rats eating bean sprouts at a premises in Pudu Market.
In a statement, the ministry said the operation would involve the Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Ministry, the Islamic Development Department of Malaysia (Jakim), the Immigration Department and Kuala Lumpur City Hall (DBKL).
It said the operation would focus on compliance with premises hygiene standards, food handling practices, raw material storage, cross-contamination risks and the effectiveness of pest control measures.
Appropriate action would be taken against any non-compliance identified under the relevant laws, it said.
The ministry said it would also intensify monitoring and follow-up action to ensure corrective measures were implemented effectively and prevent a recurrence.
"The ministry will also strengthen coordination with DBKL to ensure that market cleanliness, waste management and rat population control are addressed comprehensively.
"The ministry, through the Kuala Lumpur and Putrajaya Federal Territories Health Department, has conducted an initial inspection at the premises and found that the issues raised were substantiated.
"Traders must ensure their premises are free from pests under Regulation 16 of the Food Hygiene Regulations," it said.
The ministry said compounds could be issued for offences, while premises that posed a risk to public health could be ordered to close immediately for up to 14 days under the Food Act 1983.
It reminded traders to keep their premises clean and free of pests, store food in covered containers, manage waste properly and carry out regular rat control measures.
"Any food exposed to rats or suspected of being contaminated must be discarded and must not be sold or used for food preparation.
"The ministry also advises consumers to choose clean food that is stored in covered containers and protected from pests," it said.
The ministry also advised consumers to wash raw ingredients under clean running water and cook them thoroughly before consumption.
Complaints can be lodged through the Public Complaints Management System at moh.spab.gov.my or at the nearest district health office.
Last week, a video showing rats roaming around and
eating bean sprouts
at a premises in Pudu Market went viral.
The video, taken from a TikTok livestream, was shared by a user on Threads, raising public concern over hygiene standards at the market.
The footage purportedly showed several rats on a container filled with bean sprouts, eating its contents.

Title: Sabah SPM candidates not affected by power disruption
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: All 42,808 candidates sitting for the Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) examination in Sabah have not been affected by the electricity disruption in the state's east coast since this morning.
Sabah Education Department director Abidin Marjan said the examination, which began last Monday, had proceeded smoothly despite the power outage and flooding, particularly in Sook.
"We hope that electricity supply to the affected examination centres will be restored by tomorrow. If not, we have already prepared contingency measures to ensure that the examinations proceed smoothly.
"Most importantly, we will ensure that candidates can sit for the SPM examination comfortably and calmly, without any disruption," he told Bernama when contacted.
A total of 324 examination centres have been prepared for the candidates, with 13,291 personnel appointed to ensure the smooth conduct of this year's examination.
The department is also prioritising the safety and welfare of candidates and examination personnel through an integrated response mechanism with security and health agencies.
It has activated several contingency operations, including Ops Payung to address flood risks, Ops Topeng for haze situations, Ops Gempa for natural disasters such as earthquakes, and Ops Wabak to deal with infectious diseases.
The T313 electricity transmission tower in Ranau collapsed early this morning, affecting both transmission line circuits and disrupting electricity supply to areas along Sabah's east coast.
Eight districts experienced power disruptions after Sabah Electricity Sdn Bhd detected an incident affecting electricity transmission to the areas at 6.04am.
The Sabah Disaster Management Committee said 153 people from 42 families were still taking shelter at the temporary relief centre at the SLDB Multipurpose Hall in Kampung Dalit Gana following floods in Sook.

Title: KTMB cable theft in Penang disrupts northern train services
Article:
GEORGE TOWN: About 50 metres of cable belonging to Keretapi Tanah Melayu Berhad (KTMB) were stolen at Kilometre 16.25 of the railway line between Bukit Mertajam and Simpang Ampat.
KTMB said the theft was discovered during an inspection by its auxiliary police and have disrupted train services in the northern sector today.
"Repair and cable reconnection works are actively underway.
"KTMB, through its auxiliary police force, will continue to intensify patrols and security monitoring to protect railway infrastructure and ensure smooth train operations," it said in a Facebook post.
KTMB called on members of the public with information on any suspicious activities along railway tracks to contact the KTMB Auxiliary Police Information Collection and Dissemination Centre at 03-2263 1194 or the police for further action.

Title: 372 held, nearly RM50,000 worth of drugs seized in Perak operation
Article:
IPOH: Police detained 372 people and seized drugs worth RM49,648.30 in a three-day statewide operation from Nov 23.
Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the operation involved 25 senior officers and 223 personnel, and focused on curbing drug trafficking and abuse at identified hotspots.
He said those locations included Federal Land Development Authority schemes, Federal Land Consolidation and Rehabilitation Authority schemes, private estates, People's Housing Programme for the Hardcore Poor projects, flats and fishing jetties.
He said the detainees, aged between 14 and 70, comprised 356 men and 16 women, including 339 locals and 33 foreigners, namely 14 Thai, 13 Indonesians, five Myanmar and one Vietnamese.
"Of the total arrests, 66 people were detained for drug trafficking and 206 for drug possession, while 100 addicts are being investigated under Section 15(1)(a) of the Dangerous Drugs Act," he said in a statement.
Alwi said three wanted individuals were also arrested, while two hardcore drug addicts were identified for action under Section 39C of the Dangerous Drug Act.
He said the drug seizures in the operation involved 288.61g of ganja, syabu (251.95g), heroin (212.98g), ketamine (17.74g), Erimin 5 pills (7.46g), ketum leaves (2,300g), ketum liquid (126.10 litres) and codeine (0.18 litres).
"In addition, the Perak Narcotics Crime Investigation Department also seized a vehicle and cash totalling RM4,700.
"This success is the result of ongoing cooperation between the community and enforcement agencies," he said.
Alwi urged the public to continue providing information on drug abuse activities so enforcement action can be carried out more effectively.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Budget 2027 passage marks key step in improving lives, says Anwar
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The passage of the 2027 Budget by the Dewan Rakyat today marks an important step in the Madani government's efforts to improve the lives of the people.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the Budget also encompassed measures to strengthen the country's resilience and secure its future.
"May all the plans and initiatives outlined be implemented effectively, bring tangible benefits to the people and lay a solid foundation for building a more prosperous, equitable and harmonious Malaysia," he said in a Facebook post.
The Dewan Rakyat today passed the Supply (Budget) Bill 2027, which was tabled by Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, on Oct 9.
Themed 'Reaching for the Sky, While Anchored on Our Values', the 2027 Budget outlines eight key principles, ranging from commitments to improving the lives of the people to strengthening the country's resilience and securing its future.
The fifth budget under the Madani Government involves government allocations totalling RM459.8 billion, alongside RM25 billion in investments from government-linked investment companies (GLICs), RM11 billion in public-private investments and RM14.2 billion in investments from federal statutory bodies and Minister of Finance (Incorporated) (MOF Inc) companies.
This brings the overall size of the 2027 Budget to RM510 billion, maintaining the government's expansionary fiscal policy.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Former attorney-general Abdul Gani Patail dies at 71
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former attorney-general Tan Sri Abdul Gani Patail has died at the age of 71.
His death was confirmed by Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar to Bernama.
"He breathed his last around 9pm," he said.
Abdul Gani's second child, Faezul Adzra Patail, told Bernama that his father died at Prince Court Medical Centre at 9.15pm.
"He died due to an infection and will be laid to rest at the Precinct 20 Muslim Cemetery in Putrajaya tomorrow morning," he said.
Abdul Gani, 71, a law graduate of Universiti Malaya (UM), was the first graduate of a local university to be appointed attorney-general.
Born on Oct 6, 1955, in Lahad Datu, Sabah, he was appointed Malaysia's eighth Attorney General on Jan 1, 2002, and served until July 2015.
He joined the Judicial and Legal Service in 1980, beginning his career as a deputy public prosecutor in Kota Kinabalu, and subsequently served as senior federal counsel in Sabah, head of the Prosecution Division and Commissioner of Law Revision.
Among the high-profile cases he handled was the prosecution of 30 individuals in connection with the Lahad Datu intrusion in February 2013.
Abdul Gani led the prosecution team in the case, which involved, among others, charges of waging war against the Yang di-Pertuan Agong.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Rapid KL bus catches fire on SUKE while en route to workshop for maintenance
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: A Rapid KL bus caught fire on the Sungai Besi-Ulu Kelang Elevated Expressway (SUKE) near Bukit Segar here about 2pm today.
Rapid KL said the bus, operated by Handal Indah Sdn Bhd under Rapid Bus Sdn Bhd, was not in service when the incident occurred.
In a statement, it said preliminary information showed that the bus was being driven by a technician from the Kepong Bus Depot to a workshop in Beranang for maintenance.
"However, upon reaching the area near Bukit Segar, the bus is believed to have developed a fault before catching fire.
"The Fire and Rescue Department arrived at the scene about 15 minutes later to put out the blaze," it said.
The bus was towed to a depot in Klang at 3.28pm after firefighters confirmed that the area was safe and posed no further danger.
Rapid KL confirmed that the technician driving the bus was unharmed.
"The company will cooperate with the authorities in their investigations to determine the cause of the incident.
"An internal inspection will also be conducted to assess the condition of the bus and matters relating to its maintenance," it said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ismail Lasim remains Negri Sembilan MB, says source
Article:
SEREMBAN: Datuk Ismail Lasim will remain as Negri Sembilan menteri besar, according to a source.
The source said Ismail, who is also Juasseh assemblyman, would retain his position despite reports that he had offered to resign to resolve the state's political and administrative crisis, which has dragged on for nearly four months.
"Yes... I was informed that Datuk Mail (Ismail) will remain as menteri besar," the source said tonight.
This afternoon, Yang di-Pertuan Besar Negri Sembilan Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir
granted an audience to Ismail
at Istana Hinggap.
Tuanku Muhriz later received
a delegation of senior Umno leaders
led by Deputy Prime Minister and Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi.
Speaking to reporters after the audience, Zahid said the final decision rested with Tuanku Muhriz, adding that the delegation would
leave it to the palace
to announce the outcome of their meeting.
"We leave it to Tuanku to make the decision. The palace will issue a statement on the outcome of our discussion," he said.
As of press time, the palace has yet to issue an official statement on the menteri besar's position.
Meanwhile, several state assemblymen are scheduled
to be sworn in
as new members of the state executive council at Istana Seri Menanti in Kuala Pilah tomorrow morning.
The media have been invited to cover the ceremony.
It is understood that seven assemblymen will be appointed to the line-up.
Ismail's administration has been operating without an exco since Tuanku Muhriz revoked the appointments of all 10 members on Sept 20.
The Ruler
revoked their appointments
after the exco members maintained that the move to remove him in April was valid and that Tunku Nadzaruddin Tuanku Ja'afar was the state's new ruler.
The palace viewed their actions as being in breach of their oath of loyalty to the Ruler and the royal institution.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Power restored in parts of Sandakan, Lahad Datu and Kunak
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Electricity supply has been restored to several areas in Sandakan, Lahad Datu and Kunak tonight following an outage caused by a disruption to the transmission line from the west coast.
Sabah Electricity Sdn Bhd, in a statement, said the main areas in Sandakan where supply had been restored included Sandakan Sports Complex, Sandakan Prison, Utama Park Villa Phases 1 and 2, Garden Villa, Utama Sri Condo Blocks A and B, Utama Court, Jalan Sibuga, Taman Mawar and Taman Anggerik.
In Lahad Datu, the main areas where supply had been restored included Lahad Datu Hospital, the Eastern Sabah Security Command (Esccom) office, Lahad Datu District Office, Lahad Datu District Police Headquarters, Lahad Datu Health Clinic, Lahad Datu District Council, Fish Market, People's Market, Taman Fajar and Jalan Tengah Nipah.
In Kunak, the main areas where supply had been restored included Kunak town, Kampung Kunak Kecil, the District Office, Sime Darby Police Station, the port and surrounding areas.
"Sabah Electricity apologises for any inconvenience caused during the disruption and greatly appreciates the patience and cooperation of its customers," it said.
Meanwhile, Sabah Electricity said a viral message circulating, particularly on social media, claiming that electricity supply along Sabah's east coast would be disrupted for two weeks was fake.
The company advised the public not to be misled by viral messages, to verify information before sharing it and to obtain the latest updates only through its official platforms.
Customers seeking clarification may call 15444 or 088-515000 for verification, while enquiries or complaints can also be submitted via WhatsApp at 019-8525427.

Title: Six days to restore Sabah east coast grid, riverbank erosion caused tower collapse
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Sabah Electricity Sdn Bhd (Sabah Electricity) is targeting six days to fully restore the 275kV transmission grid supplying Sabah's east coast after a transmission tower collapsed in Ranau early today.
Its chairman, Datuk Saadiah Aziz, said the grid was expected to be fully restored by Dec 2, following the reconnection of two affected transmission lines.
She said the six-day period would allow Sabah Electricity and its contractors to transport equipment to the site, install temporary towers and reconnect the lines at a location deemed safe near the collapsed tower.
In the meantime, electricity supply to the east coast would be generated using existing power plants in Sandakan and Tawau, supplemented by mobile generators deployed to affected areas.
"We are targeting six days to reconnect the grid supplying Sabah's east coast, and the work may be completed earlier.
"However, what is important is that we also prioritise the safety of those carrying out the work on the ground.
"We hope everything goes smoothly so that electricity supply to consumers on the east coast can return to normal," she said in a press conference at Sabah Electricity's headquarters.
Also present was its chief executive officer, Datuk Mohd Yaakob Jaafar.
Saadiah said Sabah Electricity activated its crisis management system after identifying the cause of the power disruption on the east coast and immediately drew up measures to temporarily restore supply in seven affected districts.
The tower collapse disrupted electricity supply in Sandakan, Beluran, Kinabatangan, Lahad Datu, Kunak, Semporna and Tawau, affecting 153,599 registered consumers.
"We managed the situation well, beginning with the reopening of the main Ranau-Telupid road, which was blocked by an electricity cable near SK Matupang in Ranau this morning.
"This was followed by efforts to restore electricity supply in stages to the affected districts using existing and mobile generators," she said.
She said Sabah Electricity had since managed to integrate the east coast grid, connecting all districts in the region to improve supply capacity and limit scheduled power rationing to between one and two hours.
Meanwhile, Yaakob said erosion along the banks of Sungai Liwagu in Ranau, caused by strong currents following continuous rain, was identified as the main reason transmission tower T313 collapsed.
He said the riverbank erosion had been detected in January, prompting reinforcement works in March using sandbags and large rocks.
"However, strong currents in Sungai Liwagu following continuous rain in Ranau over the past few days washed away the newly reinforced riverbank, eventually causing the tower to collapse," he said.
The incident resulted in the east coast losing 295MW of electricity supplied from Sabah's west coast.
Yaakob said grid restoration would begin with the first transmission line, which was expected to be reconnected on Dec 1, followed by the second line on Dec 2, allowing Sabah's grid system to be fully restored.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Govt wants listed companies to adopt RM3,400 living wage benchmark
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The government has called on public-listed companies (PLCs) to adopt the RM3,400 living wage benchmark across their organisations.
Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said fair and adequate wages would enable employees to meet their basic needs and maintain a decent standard of living.
He said this could also contribute to greater workforce stability, better talent retention and higher productivity.
"This is an important dimension of responsible business conduct, recognising that long-term corporate value creation must also take into account the well-being and economic security of the people who contribute to it.
"Paying a living wage is verifiable proof to investors, regulators and consumers that the social pillar of your sustainability report is backed by real conviction," he said at the 2026 National Annual Corporate Report Awards (NACRA) presentation dinner.
Amir Hamzah said the government remained committed to strengthening the institutional and policy foundations for sustainable and inclusive economic growth.
"Good governance, accountability and transparency are integral to this agenda, particularly as Malaysia seeks to move towards higher-value economic activities and strengthen its position in the global economy," said Amir Hamzah.
He said stronger governance and reporting practices could help small and medium enterprises (SMEs) improve management discipline, assess business performance, access financing and engage more effectively with investors and business partners.
These capabilities are increasingly important as SMEs seek to expand their operations and participate in larger domestic and international value chains.
Amir Hamzah also said companies must invest in developing their workforce capabilities, particularly in data analytics, sustainability and environmental, social and governance (ESG) reporting, climate finance and digital finance.
"These competencies are important not only for meeting new reporting requirements, but also for understanding business risks, evaluating investment decisions and supporting long-term strategy," he added.
Meanwhile, 2026 NACRA organising committee chairman Ong Chee Wai said high-quality corporate reporting was essential to building stakeholder trust, reinforcing investor confidence and supporting sustainable business growth among Malaysian companies.
"It also provides a competitive edge, helping organisations to attract investment and compete more effectively in an increasingly interconnected global economy.
"Through NACRA, we seek to recognise organisations that demonstrate these qualities and encourage continuous improvement across the corporate sector," he said
Ong said the awards provided an opportunity for organisations to benchmark their practices against leading examples and raise the overall standard of corporate reporting in Malaysia.
Themed "Towards Accountability and Excellence", NACRA 2026 is jointly organised by Bursa Malaysia Bhd, the Malaysian Institute of Accountants and the Malaysian Institute of Certified Public Accountants.

Title: Nine Kelantan districts at risk of flooding until Nov 30
Article:
KOTA BARU: Nine districts in Kelantan are at risk of flooding until Nov 30 following a continuous rain warning issued by the Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) today.
According to the Kelantan Early Flood Forecast, updated at 8pm, the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID) identified Jeli, Pasir Mas, Tanah Merah, Tumpat, Pasir Puteh, Bachok, Kota Bharu, Machang and Kuala Krai as areas at risk.
DID said potential flood-affected areas include known flood hotspots, low-lying areas and risk zones along several major river basins in the state.
The Golok River basin covers Jeli, Pasir Mas, Tanah Merah and Tumpat, while the Kelantan River basin involves Kota Bharu, Machang and Kuala Krai.
In Pasir Puteh and Bachok, the risk areas cover the Semerak River basin, as well as the Kelantan River in Pasir Puteh and the Kemasin and Gali rivers in Bachok.
DID said continuous monitoring would be carried out, with flood warnings issued if significant rainfall persisted in the river basins.
It added that flooding could occur earlier or later than forecast.
Disaster management agencies and residents, particularly those in areas at risk, were advised to remain vigilant and follow instructions from the authorities.
The public can obtain the latest flood information and warnings via publicinfobanjir.water.gov.my and the PublicInfoBanjir Facebook page.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 'It breaks my heart': Father mourns 2 sons killed in crash
Article:
KOTA BARU: "It was heartbreaking to see my two children lying there covered in blood," said Saiful Nizam Abdul Sani, 42, whose two sons were
killed
in a motorcycle crash in Kampung Bechah Tendong, Pasir Mas, today.
His eldest son, Muhammad Saiful Haikal, 18, who was riding the motorcycle, was injured and is receiving treatment at Hospital Raja Perempuan Zainab II (HRPZ II).
Saiful Nizam said the accident occurred as Saiful Haikal was taking his two younger brothers home after picking them up from kindergarten and school.
He said the eldest had first fetched Muhammad Saiful Hayyan from kindergarten before returning home to wait until it was time to pick up Muhammad Saiful Haider from Sekolah Kebangsaan (SK) Othman Talib 1.
"When he was about to leave to collect Muhammad Saiful Haider, his younger brother also asked to go along.
"They were involved in the accident while travelling home to Kampung Bechah Tendong, about 1km from the scene," he said when met at the HRPZ II Forensic Department today.
Saiful Nizam said he received a call from his wife, Nur Zuhanis Mohd Noor, 42, about 2pm, informing him of the accident after a nearby food stall operator contacted her.
"I rushed to the scene and found two of my children lying there covered in blood. It was a heartbreaking sight.
"Saiful Haider died at the scene, while Saiful Hayyan died on the way to HRPZ II.
"Saiful Haikal is now receiving treatment at the hospital's emergency department," he said.
He also recalled that Saiful Hayyan's kindergarten teacher had noticed a change in the boy's behaviour that day, saying he had been unusually quiet.
"His teacher told me that Saiful Hayyan was usually cheerful, active and friendly, but he seemed different today," he said.
The remains of the two brothers will be buried at the Kampung Gaung Muslim cemetery in Tendong, Pasir Mas, after the post-mortem.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Genting falls into the red in Q3 with RM161.4mil net loss
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Genting Bhd posted a net loss of RM161.4 million in the third quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q3 FY26), compared with a net profit of RM30.3 million a year earlier.
Genting's quarterly revenue rose 7.3 per cent to RM8.02 billion from RM7.48 billion.
For the nine months of FY26, the group recorded a net loss of RM87.4 million, against a net profit of RM278.4 million in the corresponding period last year.
Its revenue for the nine-month period increased eight per cent to RM22.43 billion from RM20.77 billion.
Genting said the lower quarterly profit was mainly due to lower earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation (Ebitda), higher finance costs, lower interest income and a smaller share of profits from joint ventures and associates.
The group's leisure and hospitality and plantation divisions were the main contributors to revenue growth during the quarter.
However, its Resorts World Sentosa and Resorts World Genting operations recorded lower revenue and Ebitda.
Genting said it remained cautious about its near-term prospects amid geopolitical tensions, macroeconomic uncertainty and cost pressures, and would continue to focus on operational efficiency and cost discipline.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Teen believed to have lost control before crash killed 2 brothers
Article:
PASIR MAS: Police believe an 18-year-old motorcyclist lost control of his motorcycle before it crashed into a lamp post and a pothole, killing his two younger brothers in Tendong here today.
District police chief Assistant Commissioner Mazlan Hassan said the three siblings were travelling home on a Yamaha LC110 when the motorcycle skidded along the Tendong-Bunut Susu road in Kampung Bechah about 2pm.
"The impact threw all three off the motorcycle.
"The 10-year-old boy died at the scene from severe head injuries, while his six-year-old brother died while receiving treatment at the emergency department of Hospital Raja Perempuan Zainab II (HRPZ II) in Kota Baru," he said.
Mazlan said the eldest brother, who was riding the motorcycle, sustained head injuries and remained under treatment at the same hospital.
The case is being investigated under Section 41(1) of the Road Transport Act 1987.
He reminded parents to pay closer attention to their children's road safety and ensure they wear helmets when riding motorcycles.
He also cautioned against carrying more than two people on a motorcycle, saying the practice was illegal and posed a safety risk.
"Police will continue enforcement operations to ensure road users comply with traffic regulations, while educating the public on the importance of road safety," he said.
Earlier NST reported that
two siblings were killed
while their 18-year-old brother was injured when the motorcycle they were riding skidded and overturned in Tendong.

Title: Discipline teacher cleared of physical assault, jailed over sexual remarks
Article:
TAWAU: A secondary school discipline teacher was acquitted by the Sessions Court today of physically sexually assaulting a 17-year-old student four years ago.
However, he was sentenced to two years in prison and two strokes of the rotan for non-physical sexual assault involving another student.
Judge Ahmad Faizadh Yahaya imposed a one-year jail term for the offence, with an additional one-year jail term and two strokes of the cane under Section 16 of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017.
The court took into account that the 37-year-old accused was a teacher who held a position of trust over the victim.
On the first charge, the accused was alleged to have physically sexually assaulted a 17-year-old student in the library of a secondary school here around noon on Feb 15, 2022.
The charge was framed under Section 14(a) of the Sexual Offences Against Children Act 2017, read together with Section 16 of the same Act.
In his judgment, Faizadh said there was reasonable doubt over whether the accused had access to the library, where the alleged offence took place.
He said the accused's denial of having access to the room was supported by documents showing that he had been assigned to mark Sijil Pelajaran Malaysia (SPM) examination papers at the time.
The court therefore ruled that the defence had succeeded in raising reasonable doubt over the first charge, before acquitting and discharging him at the close of the defence case.
On the second charge, the accused was alleged to have committed non-physical sexual assault by making sexually explicit remarks and holding and pulling the hand of another 17-year-old student for sexual purposes at the same location about 9.20am on April 19, 2022.
The charge was framed under Section 15(a) of Act 792, read together with Section 16 of the same Act.
Faizadh said it was undisputed that the accused held a position of trust over the victim and was the only teacher who was not attached to the library but had permission to use it and hold its keys at the time.
He said the court found that the victim's testimony on the sexually explicit remarks and the act of pulling her hand remained consistent and was not shaken during cross-examination by the defence.
The judge also noted that the accused had admitted to touching the victim's hand when handing over a mobile phone.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Opposition leader questions Achi Jaya's Boustead Plantations bid
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Opposition leader Datuk Seri Hamzah Zainudin says it is against the proposed takeover of Boustead Plantations Bhd by Achi Jaya Plantations Sdn Bhd, questioning the prospect of a strategic plantation asset coming under foreign ownership.
Hamzah said the opposition will not support the proposed sale, claiming that Boustead Plantations was set to be acquired by a company owned by foreigners.
He said the development was concerning, particularly after an earlier attempt to sell part of the plantation group's stake to a Malaysian company had faced opposition from the then opposition bloc.
"Today, there is something else happening. Boustead already has an agreement, and we have heard from sources within the country that Boustead Plantations will be sold to a company owned by 'foreigners'.
"We, the opposition, do not agree with this at all," he said.
Hamzah added that the opposition will issue a formal statement to register its objection to the proposed transaction.
His remarks come after reports that the Armed Forces Fund Board (LTAT) had selected Achi Jaya Plantations to acquire Boustead Plantations in a deal estimated at RM4.3 billion.
Achi Jaya reportedly emerged ahead of competing bidders SD Guthrie Bhd and Tradewinds Plantation Bhd, both of which have substantially larger plantation operations.
The reported selection has raised questions over the evaluation criteria used by LTAT, particularly given the scale of the bidders and their respective operational track records.
Pasir Mas MP Ahmad Fadhli Shaari had also called on LTAT to explain why Achi Jaya was preferred over the two larger plantation groups.
Achi Jaya is a privately held company incorporated in 2001, with interests in oil palm cultivation and milling, as well as hotel management and operations.
According to its November 2025 Malaysian Sustainable Palm Oil certification audit, the company's operations within the scope of certification comprised 11,702 hectares of oil palm planted area across three estates in Johor.
In comparison, Boustead Plantations has a land bank of 97,500 hectares, including about 72,200 hectares of planted oil palm areas.
The acquisition could therefore significantly expand Achi Jaya's plantation footprint, although the actual scale of the combined operations would depend on the assets and equity interests covered by the transaction.
A check on Achi Jaya's shareholding structure reportedly found links to Tan Sri Onn Mahmud, the younger brother of former Sarawak chief minister and governor Tun Abdul Taib Mahmud.
Grand Shine Trading Ltd and Herolite Investment Ltd each hold 36.89 per cent stakes in Achi Jaya, while Onn's company, Achi Jaya Holdings, holds 14.3 per cent.
Onn also has a direct 11.91 per cent interest in the company.
The proposed takeover comes three years after an earlier attempt to sell a 33 per cent stake in Boustead Plantations to Kuala Lumpur Kepong Bhd (KLK) for RM1.15 billion was terminated in October 2023.
The proposed transaction had valued Boustead Plantations at RM3.47 billion, but faced political resistance over concerns that LTAT would relinquish control of a strategic plantation asset to a non-Bumiputera company.
The latest reported RM4.3 billion price tag is about RM830 million, or 23.9 per cent, higher than the valuation under the previous KLK proposal, although a direct comparison would depend on the final transaction structure and the equity interest involved.

Title: Teen gets warning after admitting to cyberbullying
Article:
TAWAU: An 18-year-old student who pleaded guilty to uploading a 13-year-old girl's photograph on social media with threatening captions was discharged with a warning by the magistrate's court today.
Magistrate Don Stiwin Malanjum made the ruling under Section 91(1)(a) of the Child Act 2001 (Amendment 2016) after taking into account recommendations from the Social Welfare Department.
The court also considered that the eldest of five siblings regretted his actions, had promised not to reoffend and wanted to focus on his studies.
The court also ordered the return of his RM500 bail.
According to the charge, the accused, who was 17 at the time of the offence, had uploaded the photograph of the victim, then 13, at a restaurant at noon on April 17.
He was charged under Section 507E of the Penal Code, which carries a maximum prison term of 20 years and whipping upon conviction.
Based on the facts of the case, the victim's mother received a WhatsApp message from a friend containing a screenshot of her daughter's photograph on Instagram, accompanied by several captions making allegations of bullying and threats.
Investigations found that the accused had uploaded the photograph after reading a WhatsApp group conversation claiming that a friend's cousin had been bullied by the victim and another individual.
The accused admitted that he had acted on impulse before obtaining the victim's photograph and uploading it to his Instagram Story with threatening captions.
Prosecuting Officer ASP Jeffery Kadison prosecuted, while the accused was unrepresented.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: 11 foreigners held over NYPD impersonation scam in KL
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Police have arrested 11 foreigners suspected of running an international online scam by posing as New York police officers in Bukit Ceylon on Tuesday.
The raid was conducted by Dang Wangi police at 5pm on Tuesday.
It followed information and intelligence gathered on a scam targeting victims in the United States.
Dang Wangi police chief Assistant Commissioner Ahmad Azwan Amin Nordin said those arrested were aged between 22 and 51 and comprised four South Africans, three Taiwanese, and one each from Mexico, Zimbabwe, Kenya and India.
"In the same operation, the raiding team seized three sets of New York Police Department (NYPD) uniforms, a New York police logo signboard and a map of New York City, which were used to deceive victims contacted through video calls.
"Also seized were 31 mobile phones, seven laptops, a monitor, a computer CPU and a router," he told a press conference today.
Azwan said digital forensic examinations and social media analysis of the seized devices indicated that the syndicate was suspected of carrying out scams by impersonating NYPD officers.
Investigations found that the suspects used artificial intelligence (AI) technology, including face-swapping techniques, background images and documents resembling official NYPD records, to convince victims that they were genuine police officers.
He said the syndicate used internet access to carry out online scams and was believed to have been operating since the middle of this year.
"The syndicate's modus operandi was to deceive victims by claiming they were involved in criminal activities and money laundering.
"All those arrested have been remanded for four days, from Nov 25 to 28," he said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Dewan Rakyat passes 2027 Budget
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: The Dewan Rakyat today passed the Supply (Budget) Bill 2027 by a majority voice vote.
Deputy Speaker Datuk Seri Dr Ramli Mohd Nor announced its passage after the Bill was tabled for its third reading by Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan.
The Bill was tabled by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim on Oct 9.
Themed "Reaching for the Sky, Rooted on the Ground", the 2027 Budget outlines eight key pillars, focusing on improving people's lives and strengthening the country's resilience and future.
The fifth budget under the Madani government involves a government allocation of RM459.8 billion, alongside RM25 billion in investments from government-linked investment companies (GLICs), RM11 billion in public-private investments, and RM14.2 billion in investments by federal statutory bodies and Minister of Finance Incorporated companies.
This brings the total allocation and investments under the 2027 Budget to RM510 billion, maintaining an expansionary fiscal policy.
The Dewan Rakyat will resume its sitting on Monday.

Title: Tengku Ampuan Afzan Hospital to reorganise parking, introduce valet service
Article:
KUANTAN: The Health Ministry has appointed a private company to reorganise parking at Tengku Ampuan Afzan Hospital (HTAA), provide valet services and introduce parking fees as early as March.
Pahang Public Works, Transport and Health Committee chairman Datuk Razali Kassim said the company was appointed effective Nov 1 to reorganise existing parking facilities and increase capacity for hospital staff and visitors.
He said upgrading works on existing parking facilities within the hospital compound would be carried out during the first three months.
Parking fees were expected to be introduced as early as March next year, based on rates approved by the ministry, he said during his winding-up speech at the Pahang State Legislative Assembly sitting today.
The company would also be responsible for building and managing a multi-storey mechanical parking facility, with construction scheduled to begin in April next year and finish by July.
The valet service would help patients' family members find parking spaces more quickly and conveniently.
HTAA, Pahang's largest healthcare facility, currently has only 160 public parking bays, which are insufficient to meet demand.
The proposed
mechanical parking facility
is expected to provide an additional 600 bays.
Meanwhile, Razali said construction of the new women's and
children's block
in Tanjung Lumpur was 25 per cent complete as of October and scheduled for completion in December 2028.
The 376-bed block is being built at a cost of RM605 million.

Title: Power restored in parts of Tawau, Semporna and Telupid
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: Electricity supply was restored to several areas in Tawau, Semporna and Telupid this afternoon following an outage caused by a disruption to the transmission line from the West Coast.
Sabah Electricity Sdn Bhd said the areas in Tawau where supply had been restored included the Health Ministry clinic office and quarters, Taman Ambar Park, Taman Kuhara Jaya, Taman Hilltop along Jalan Kuhara and Hilltop Supermarket.
Other areas included the United Armed Forces Camp and 516 Territorial Army Camp, Taman Ria 1 to 9, Uni Park Industrial, Taman Jen Loong and Taman Bunga Tulip.
Supply was also restored to SMK Tawau, SMK Holy Trinity and SK Holy Trinity, as well as Gaya Commercial Centre, SUDC Commercial Centre along Jalan Kuhara and Promenade Hotel.
In Semporna, the main areas where supply had been restored included Semporna Hospital and its quarters, Bandar Seri Melur and the water village areas, as well as coastal areas including Kampung Bangau-Bangau, Kampung Panji and Kampung Air.
In Telupid, supply had been restored at Maxis Batu 4, Kampung Gaab and Kampung Gansad 01.
"Sabah Electricity greatly appreciates your patience and sincerely regrets any inconvenience caused," it said, apologising for the disruption and expressing appreciation for customers' patience and cooperation.
Meanwhile, authorities and telecommunications service providers have implemented mitigation measures to maintain connectivity along Sabah's east coast following the power disruption.
These include activating backup Starlink connections at 18 critical sites and deploying mobile and shared generator sets at 20 locations.
Sabah Electricity also shared a list of hotspot connection locations to support telecommunications service continuity, while telecommunications service providers have identified collector sites along the east coast to be prioritised for restoration.
Relevant teams have begun deploying generator sets in stages to priority sites, including critical locations and collector sites.
Sabah Electricity also implemented scheduled rotational power rationing along Sabah's east coast today due to limited local generation capacity following the T313 transmission tower incident.

Title: From remote Batang Rajang to luxury tables: Sarawak’s prized empurau commands up to RM2,500 per kg
Article:
SIBU, Nov 26 — The landing of an empurau weighing over 12 kilogrammes at the premises of Sarawak wild fish supplier Jeferry Siew Seng Kwong here proves that the species is not merely an ordinary river catch, but a luxury commodity worth tens of thousands of ringgit.
Known scientifically as Tor tambroides, the fish, which fetches RM2,000 to RM2,500 per kilogramme in the international market, continues to cement its dominance in the exclusive culinary segment.
The iconic species is now sought after by high-end restaurants, wholesalers, and the elite in Hong Kong, China, and Singapore, as well as the Peninsular Malaysia market including Kuala Lumpur, Perak, and Penang.
Behind that extraordinary price tag, the journey of the “King of the River” begins far in the remote upstream areas before passing through a chain of fishermen, suppliers, and air logistics to reach the dining tables of high-income earners.
For Jeferry, 41, the business is not merely about chasing profits through trading exotic fish, but also ensuring that every bit of hard work by local fishermen receives a fair and lucrative return.
“This empurau has its own uniqueness with fine, tender, and sweet-textured flesh as well as a fatty belly, while its special aroma comes from its natural diet as it feeds only on wild forest fruits such as engkabang and ensurai.
“A large-sized fish can fetch tens of thousands of ringgit, even enough to buy an used car, depending on its weight and the market,” he told Bernama recently.
He said the uniqueness of the empurau, which inhabits fast-flowing upstream rivers, also lies in its growth period, which takes more than 10 years.
Fresh supplies are obtained directly from fishermen’s bases in the interior such as Ulu Kapit and Baleh, with the nearly 600-kilometre Batang Rajang river basin remaining the main habitat for various high-value freshwater species.
Close cooperation with local fishermen, including Leanard Anak Lenggie and Gamas Iban from Kapit, forms the backbone of his operational stability, which demands swift action as soon as the catch is brought ashore.
He said in the wild fish trade, there is no room for any delay as timeliness is the absolute determining factor in maintaining the freshness and highest-grade quality of the empurau.
He noted that demand for the premium species usually surges ahead of festive seasons such as Christmas and Chinese New Year to be served as a special dish for families and celebratory gatherings.
Apart from empurau, Jeferry’s business premises located at Jalan Long Bridge also supply various other freshwater species including patin buah, tapah, jelawat, semah, tengadak, terubuk, sebarau, giant freshwater prawns (udang galah), ketutu, and baung.
This variety allows his business to cater to the tastes and budgets of customers from various backgrounds, rather than relying on empurau alone.
Commenting on export matters, Jeferry said shipments outside Sarawak via air freight to maintain freshness also affect the selling price, in addition to requiring permits, veterinary documents, and shipping declarations.
His experience in managing shipping as well as import-export businesses has also been an advantage in handling documentation and logistics coordination to meet customer needs.
Ahead of the 13th Sarawak State Election, the Sibu native, who will cast his ballot in the Bukit Assek state constituency, hopes the potential of the river fisheries sector, particularly high-value species like empurau, will be given due attention by elected representatives as one of the state’s economic drivers.
He said continuous support in terms of infrastructure, basic amenities, and market access is crucial to ensure Sarawak’s river produce continues to bring greater benefits to fishing communities and the rural economy.
“I believe efforts to strengthen market access, transport facilities, as well as networks between operators and suppliers also have the potential to help this sector grow, thereby ensuring Sarawak’s river produce continues to secure a place in both domestic and international premium markets,” he said.
Bukit Assek is one of two state constituencies in the Lanang parliamentary constituency, alongside Dudong, involved in the Sarawak State Election.
The Election Commission (EC) has set this Saturday (November 28) as nomination day, followed by early voting on December 8 and polling day on December 12.
