Title: Cybersecurity gets its own priority in Malaysia’s new National Security Policy
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today launched the National Security Policy 2026–2030, outlining Malaysia’s security priorities for the next five years, with a new strategic focus on cybersecurity and technology.
The policy takes into account changes in the geopolitical landscape and increasingly complex traditional and non-traditional security threats, aiming to strengthen the country’s preparedness against emerging challenges.
Anwar said the policy adopts a Comprehensive Security approach, covering politics, the economy, society, the environment, public safety and technology, supported by collaboration between government agencies, the private sector, academia, non-governmental organisations and the public.
“Our approach and outlook towards security threats have changed.
“We are no longer dealing solely with conventional forces or threats originating from other countries or within the region.
“This underscores the need to strengthen our cybersecurity capabilities, including investing in training and developing infrastructure to address new and increasingly unpredictable threats,” he said in his speech.
Anwar said security threats were no longer confined to conventional conflicts between countries, with cyberattacks increasingly targeting financial systems, defence networks and critical infrastructure.
“The National Security Policy takes into account the perspectives of previous policies, but I believe its strength lies in its ability to anticipate and address new issues and challenges,” he said.
He urged relevant ministries to consider setting up dedicated units to strengthen national capabilities, particularly in cybersecurity, while improving coordination between agencies.
He said these efforts must be supported by specialised expertise, including providing young officers with exposure and specialised training at leading institutions worldwide.
The National Security Policy 2026–2030 is a continuation of the previous 2021–2025 policy, which was based on the Comprehensive Security concept.
Under the latest policy, the previous nine National Security Core Values have been reorganised into 10 Strategic Focus Areas, including Sovereignty and Territorial Integrity, Sociopolitical Stability, National Cohesion, Effective Governance, Economic Resilience, Social Justice, Sustainable Development, People's Security, Security Diplomacy and Regional Cooperation, and Cybersecurity and Technology.
The last category is a new addition, reflecting the growing importance of cybersecurity and technological threats in national security planning.
The policy identifies 53 security issues, challenges and threats, which will be addressed through 30 strategies across the 10 focus areas.
Its implementation will be coordinated by the National Security Council under the Prime Minister’s Department, together with relevant ministries and agencies, with cooperation from the private sector and the public.
Monitoring mechanisms include National Security Council meetings, coordination and implementation monitoring committees, the National Security Index, security exercises and simulations, and integrated operations.

Title: No reduction: Deputy minister clears the air over RM1b Education Ministry budget cut claims
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — The Ministry of Education (MOE) has denied claims that the government had cut its development allocation by RM1 billion in Budget 2027, saying that the amount had been transferred to its operating expenditure before it was agreed that the allocation would be restored.
Deputy Education Minister Wong Kah Woh said following MOE’s application to the Ministry of Finance (MOF), the ministry’s development allocation would increase to RM6.515 billion from the previous RM5.515 billion.
“This does not involve a reduction in the allocation. The amount was merely transferred, and the ministry had applied to the MOF to have it returned to the development allocation, to which the MOF has agreed.
“Therefore, the MOE’s development allocation will now increase to RM6.515 billion from the previous RM5.515 billion, representing an increase of RM200 million compared with the 2026 development allocation,” he said.
He said this when winding up the debate on the Supply Bill (Budget) 2027 and the 2027 Development Expenditure Estimates motion at the committee stage for the MOE in the Dewan Rakyat today.
During the same session, he also denied allegations by Datuk Rosol Wahid (PN-Hulu Terengganu) that the tender for the production and supply of Jalur Gemilang badges distributed by the MOE to all students in 2025 had been awarded to friends and cronies.
Wong said all procurement processes were carried out by State Education Departments and District Education Offices through the ePerolehan system, either through tenders or quotations, depending on the allocation received.
“I am disappointed by this allegation. I hope Hulu Terengganu will withdraw his allegation that the project was awarded to friends or cronies. Do not make allegations against government officers who handled the matter, and do not drag them into political games,” he said.
In another development, Wong said the placement of 3,150 contract-of-service (COS) teachers recruited to help prepare for the admission of six-year-old pupils into Standard One would be announced on Dec 7.
He said the teachers would undergo training at Teacher Education Institutes (IPGs) until Dec 23 in preparation for their duties in the 2027 school session.
On the readiness of educational facilities to accommodate the needs of more than 73,000 six-year-old Standard One pupils in the 2027 school session, Wong said so far, 1,040 additional classrooms were ready for use, comprising 639 classrooms created through renovation or upgrading works and 401 modular classrooms built using the Industrialised Building System (IBS).
“The MOE projects that an additional 2,050 classrooms created through renovation and upgrading works, as well as 1,470 modular classrooms using the IBS method, will be completed by year-end, bringing the total to 3,520 classrooms ready for use in the upcoming school session,” he said.
Meanwhile, he said all 17 schools selected for the pilot Autism Classroom Model (MKA) would begin operations in the upcoming school session, with the ministry aiming to expand the programme to 30 schools nationwide in the future.
The Dewan Rakyat subsequently approved the RM68,988,501,800 in operating and development expenditure allocated to the MOE under Budget 2027, with a majority vote, following debate by 33 Members of Parliament. — Bernama

Title: Negeri Sembilan exco swearing-in ceremony set for 9am tomorrow
Article:
SEREMBAN, Nov 26 — The swearing-in ceremony for the new Negeri Sembilan State Executive Council (Exco) members is scheduled to take place at Istana Besar Seri Menanti in Kuala Pilah tomorrow.
According to a media invitation issued by the palace, the ceremony will be held at 9am.
Earlier today, Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi had an audience with the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, at Istana Hinggap here to discuss the ongoing political crisis in the state.
The meeting, which lasted about an hour, was also attended by Umno deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan, Barisan Nasional secretary-general Datuk Seri Dr Zambry Abd Kadir, Umno secretary-general Datuk Dr Asyraf Wajdi Dusuki and Umno Information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
Also present was Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim. — Bernama

Title: IGP says police investigating Tony Pua over Najib pardon post, Khoo Poay Tiong over Friday prayer remarks
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Former Damansara MP Tony Pua and incumbent Kota Melaka MP Khoo Poay Tiong are under police investigation over their Facebook posts.
Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said the two DAP politicians are being investigated separately, with Pua related to the declassification of documents relating to former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak’s pardon, Khoo on the closure of businesses in Kuala Terengganu during Friday prayers.
“Firm action without compromise will be taken against any party who deliberately makes or spreads statements that may cause public alarm,” he said in a statement this evening, adding that 55 reports had been filed over Pua’s post and two over Khoo’s remarks.
Both investigations are being handled by the Classified Criminal Investigation Unit under the Prosecution and Legal Division (D5) of the Criminal Investigation Department at Bukit Aman.
Pua’s case is being investigated under Section 203A of the Penal Code for disclosing information, which carries a fine of up to RM1 million, up to one year’s jail, or both.
It is also being investigated under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 for improper use of network facilities or services, which carries a fine of up to RM500,000, up to two years’ jail, or both.
Khoo’s case is being investigated under Section 298 of the Penal Code for deliberately intending to wound the religious feelings of any person, which carries up to one year’s jail, a fine, or both.
It is also being investigated under Section 505(b) of the Penal Code for statements that could cause public mischief by creating public fear or alarm, which carries up to two years’ jail, a fine, or both.
Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 has also been invoked in Khoo’s case.
Mohd Khalid said both cases were still at the investigation stage.
“The cases are still at the investigation stage, and police remind the public not to make speculation that could disrupt the investigation process,” he said.
He also urged all parties to steer clear of 3R, which stands for race, religion and royalty.
“Police also warn all parties not to ever touch on or raise 3R issues in any form that could jeopardise the peace and harmony of Malaysian society,” he said.
Pua posted on Facebook on November 18 what he said were declassified minutes of the Federal Territories Pardons Board’s September 18 meeting on Najib’s house arrest.
The pages reportedly recorded objections by Attorney-General Tan Sri Mohd Dusuki Mokhtar and Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh to Najib serving the rest of his sentence under house arrest.
Umno information chief Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said demanded to know whether the minutes had been formally declassified, saying such a decision had to be made under Section 2C of the Official Secrets Act 1972.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the document may have been declassified for court proceedings.
Khoo, who is also Melaka DAP chairman, questioned on November 20 a Kuala Terengganu City Council directive requiring businesses to close from 12.30pm to 2.30pm on Fridays, saying it affected non-Muslim traders.
He apologised the next day, and the Melaka government accepted the apology on November 23.

Title: Three RMAF officers among six to be charged in Shah Alam tomorrow over drug smuggling using military assets
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Six individuals, comprising three Royal Malaysian Air Force (RMAF) officers and three civilians, will be charged at the Shah Alam Magistrate’s Court tomorrow in connection with a drug smuggling case involving the use of military assets.
Bukit Aman Narcotics Crime Investigation Department (NCID) director Datuk Hussein Omar Khan said all six suspects would be charged under Section 39B of the Dangerous Drugs Act 1952 following the referral of the investigation papers to the Attorney General’s Chambers.
He said action would be taken against seven other suspects arrested in connection with the case under the Dangerous Drugs (Special Preventive Measures) Act 1985.
“All 13 suspects, comprising seven RMAF officers and personnel and six civilians, were arrested during a joint operation by the NCID and the RMAF Provost Marshal Branch from November 17 to 19,” he said in a statement today.
The media previously reported that the cross-border drug smuggling syndicate was uncovered after 96.64 kilogrammes of suspected methamphetamine worth RM4.83 million and 6.98 kilogrammes of chemicals were discovered as they were about to be loaded onto an RMAF aircraft at the Subang Air Base.
Following the discovery, a series of raids was conducted in the Klang Valley, Labuan and at a military base in Tawau, Sabah, leading to the arrest of all 13 suspects.
The syndicate is believed to have been active since July this year, exploiting military air transport facilities to smuggle drugs from Peninsular Malaysia to Sabah before distributing them to international markets, including the Philippines and Indonesia. — Bernama

Title: Diplomacy first on Myanmar refugees and South China Sea, Anwar says at national security policy launch
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today emphasised the importance of diplomacy in addressing regional security challenges, stressing the need to maintain strong ties with neighbouring countries.
Speaking at the launch of the National Security Policy 2026 to 2030 today, Anwar said Malaysia must prioritise diplomacy and maintain good relations with its neighbours to address regional security challenges while ensuring its own defence capabilities remain strong.
This includes maintaining diplomatic engagement with Myanmar to address longstanding issues surrounding the repatriation of refugees from Myanmar in Malaysia, as well as pushing, through Asean, for a Code of Conduct on the South China Sea.
“When my fellow ministers discuss whether we should maintain good relations with Myanmar’s government, my answer is yes.
“Why? Because it is necessary to resolve many of the problems we are facing.
“The issue involving 200,000 Myanmar nationals in Malaysia cannot be resolved by international organisations or foreign countries, regardless of how extensively they discuss the matter. We have to resolve it ourselves,” Anwar said.
Anwar said Malaysia is also seeking assurances from Myanmar that the safety of those being repatriated would be guaranteed and that their situation could be monitored upon their return.
He stressed that the government was not sending them back to face harm, adding that failing to address the issue would place a greater financial burden on Malaysia and potentially worsen public frustration and security concerns.
Malaysia has faced international criticism over its approach to the refugee issue involving Myanmar.
“Sometimes, refugees are unable to find employment, and this can contribute to an increase in crime-related issues, for example.
“That is why, in my view, discussions on national security must also take into account the wisdom of maintaining good diplomatic relations with neighbouring and regional countries,” Anwar said.
On the South China Sea dispute, Anwar stressed that Malaysia would continue to pursue diplomatic negotiations with China through Asean while strengthening its defence capabilities to safeguard the country’s maritime interests and sovereignty.
He said that Malaysia would continue working with Asean to pursue negotiations with China and push for the finalisation of a South China Sea Code of Conduct, which he said should be anchored in the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea 1982.
“I am not suggesting that Malaysia does not face problems.
“Malaysia is a maritime nation, and we have issues involving our neighbours and our maritime boundaries.
“However, the existence of these issues does not mean we are enemies or that they should lead to tensions in our bilateral relations,” Anwar said.
He added that Chinese Premier Li Qiang had also agreed to step up efforts towards finalising the Code of Conduct during the recent Asean meeting.
Asean and China missed their 2026 target for concluding the code but have reaffirmed their commitment to expedite the talks, with no new deadline set.
“Our Navy must always be prepared. We have consistently reminded them that defence is a major responsibility, and they must remain vigilant and maintain control over our waters.
“But we have not experienced the kind of confrontations seen in the Philippines, nor have we been involved in similar incidents.
“I have chosen the diplomatic path, although I agree with the calls made by the defence minister and the Defence Ministry for us to strengthen our capabilities and readiness to safeguard our national interests,” Anwar said.
The launch of the National Security Policy 2026 to 2030 was also attended by Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin, Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail, and National Security Council director-general Datuk Raja Nushirwan Zainal Abidin.

Title: Budget 2027 sails through Dewan Rakyat by voice vote, four weeks after Anwar’s CSA deal
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — The Dewan Rakyat today passed the Supply Bill 2027 via a voice vote at its third reading, capping weeks of committee-stage debate.
This is Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim’s fifth and biggest federal budget, although development spending is still lower than the record allocation announced for 2023, at RM97 billion.
Deputy Speaker Datuk Seri Ramli Mohd Nor declared the Bill approved late this afternoon after the Ministry of Youth and Sports wrapped up the final round of debates.
No Opposition MPs rose to call for bloc voting.
As a voice vote does not record a head count, the outcome does not show how many MPs backed the Bill.
Anwar, who is also finance minister, was present in the House alongside some senior ministers.
The RM459.8 billion spending plan comes to RM510 billion when investments from government-linked investment companies, statutory bodies, Minister of Finance Incorporated companies and public-private partnerships are factored in.
It passes ahead of a potential general election that might be called next year.
Of the RM459.8 billion direct federal allocation, RM376.8 billion is earmarked for operating expenditure while RM83 billion goes toward development.
Today’s uncontested vote was largely telegraphed following a Confidence and Supply Agreement (CSA) inked on October 29 between the Anwar administration and 13 MPs.
The CSA, announced the same day the Bill cleared its policy stage, was signed by six Bersatu MPs led by party president Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin, six former Bersatu MPs and Muda’s Muar MP Syed Saddiq Syed Abdul Rahman.
Under the pact, the signatories will back the budget and Anwar’s administration in return for the same constituency allocations as government backbenchers.
The agreement also covers institutional reforms, including limiting the prime minister’s tenure to two terms and separating the powers of the attorney general and public prosecutor.
Anwar had previously confirmed that constituency allocations for the 13 signatories would be disbursed upon the Supply Bill’s final approval in Parliament.

Title: DAP still contesting Sarawak polls, but non-Sarawakian ministers to stay off campaign trail, says Chong Chieng Jen
Article:
KUCHING, Nov 26 — DAP will go ahead and contest the state election, but non-Sarawakian DAP leaders who hold federal minister or deputy minister posts will stay out of the campaign, its state chief Chong Chieng Jen said today.
Chong said he met DAP secretary-general Anthony Loke following PKR’s decision to pull out of the polls, and that after a long discussion the party reached a clear consensus.
“Sarawak DAP decides for Sarawak,” he said in a press statement.
He said Sarawak DAP maintains its position to contest whichever seats it decides on in the coming election.
Chong said this was not a new concession but a principle the state chapter has always upheld, including the number of seats, the choice of candidates and the signing of the watikah to contest under the DAP logo.
He said the DAP Central Executive Committee has reaffirmed that it fully respects this autonomy and will abide by the arrangement within the party.
On the federal office holders, Chong said they will not take part in the campaign “in the spirit of the Madani Government, and out of respect for our coalition partners at the federal level”.
“Sarawak DAP will lead the campaign on the ground, with our own leaders, our own members and our own message,” he said.
Chong said yesterday that DAP would contest despite PKR sitting out, arguing that a stronger opposition was needed to keep Gabungan Parti Sarawak in check.
Sarawak DAP has finalised a 12-seat line-up for the polls.
Umno and Perikatan Nasional have also said they will not contest.
On November 15, Loke said DAP had given Sarawak DAP full autonomy to decide the number of seats, candidates and strategy for the election.
Nominations are on November 28, with polling on December 12.

Title: Hannah Yeoh’s pol-sec says ‘nothing to hide’ after giving MACC statement on KLSCAH lease
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Political secretary Yap Yee Vonne has said that nothing wrong was done in extending the Kuala Lumpur and Selangor Chinese Assembly Hall (KLSCAH) land lease, after assisting a Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) investigation into the matter today.
Yap, who is political secretary to Federal Territories Minister Hannah Yeoh, said she attended MACC’s Putrajaya headquarters with lawyer Sangeet Kaur Deo to help with the probe.
“We did nothing wrong, and we have nothing to hide or fear,” she said in a Facebook statement.
She said she gave her full cooperation throughout the statement-recording process and remains ready to provide any further information or clarification if MACC requires it.
Yap pointed to Yeoh’s explanation in the Dewan Rakyat, saying the decision was made after due consideration and in accordance with established procedures.
She also thanked MACC officers for their professionalism, saying she recognised they were merely carrying out their duties and fully respected their role.
“Nevertheless, I must emphasise that MACC’s resources and attention should be directed towards more pressing matters of public interest,” she said.
“KLSCAH is a heritage institution of historical and cultural significance that deserves our collective support and protection, not continued controversy,” she added.
Earlier today, MACC confirmed it had recorded a statement from a minister’s aide to assist its investigation into the lease renewal under Section 23 of the MACC Act 2009, which deals with abuse of power.
The probe stems from Yeoh’s announcement at KLSCAH’s 103rd anniversary dinner on November 14 that the government had approved a 99-year lease renewal for the hall at a nominal land premium of RM1,000, down from an earlier estimated premium of about RM4.67 million.
The minister said the land’s status had been changed to institutional use, meaning it could no longer be developed for projects such as condominiums or shopping malls.
The decision drew criticism, including from Umno Youth chief Datuk Dr Akmal Saleh, who challenged Yeoh to name a single plot of land in Kuala Lumpur that had no value.
Yeoh has defended the decision in the Dewan Rakyat, saying seven other organisations in the city had also received nominal premiums of RM1,000.

Title: Top 10 and counting: Anwar makes the cut in Asia Power Index
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has been ranked among the global top 10 leaders for effective political leadership in the Lowy Institute’s 2026 Asia Power Index.
The latest report, which assesses the effectiveness of political leaders in advancing their countries’ diplomatic interests internationally, placed Anwar 10th globally with a score of 46 points, according to a post on Australia’s ABC Asia Facebook page.
Regionally, he was one of only three Asean leaders to make the global top 10, alongside Singapore’s Prime Minister Lawrence Wong, who ranked third with 74 points, and Vietnam’s President To Lam, who placed eighth with 50 points.
Chinese President Xi Jinping topped the political leadership rankings in the 2026 Asia Power Index, scoring 100 out of 100 for global diplomatic effectiveness.
Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi ranked second, while Japan’s Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese placed fourth and fifth, respectively.
Compiled by Australian think tank the Lowy Institute, the rankings are based on a survey of experts assessing how effectively political leaders advance their countries’ diplomatic interests on the global stage.
The political leadership rankings form part of the broader Asia Power Index, which measures the power and influence of 27 countries and territories across the region. — Bernama

Title: Tawau, Sandakan, Lahad Datu airports keep flying on gensets after outage
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Nov 26 — Operations at Tawau, Sandakan and Lahad Datu airports remain normal despite a power supply disruption on Sabah’s east coast, with all three airports currently running on generator sets (gensets).
Malaysia Airports Holdings Berhad (Malaysia Airports) said the outage affected the three airports following electricity supply disruptions reported by Sabah Electricity in several areas of the state.
“All three airports are operating on gensets to ensure continuity of power supply while maintaining normal operations,” it said in a statement on its official Facebook page today.
Malaysia Airports added that it would continue to monitor the situation closely and provide updates as necessary.
Electricity transmission tower T313 in Ranau collapsed early this morning, affecting both transmission line circuits and disrupting electricity supply to Sabah’s east coast.
Eight districts on Sabah’s east coast experienced a power outage after Sabah Electricity detected an incident involving electricity transmission to the affected areas at 6.04 am.
The affected districts were Tawau, Sandakan, Semporna, Lahad Datu, Kunak, Beluran, Telupid and Kinabatangan. — Bernama

Title: Heads up: Heavy rain and strong winds forecast for KL, Penang and eight other states tonight
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued a warning of thunderstorms, heavy rain and strong winds across 10 states and Kuala Lumpur until 8 pm tonight.
MetMalaysia, in a statement issued at 4.30 pm, said the warning covers all of Penang and Kuala Lumpur, as well as seven districts in Kedah, namely Kuala Muda, Sik, Pendang, Yan, Baling, Kulim and Bandar Baharu.
In Perak, the warning covers Kerian, Selama, Larut Matang, Hulu Perak, Kuala Kangsar, Kinta, Kampar, Batang Padang and Muallim.
In Selangor, it affects Hulu Langat, Hulu Selangor and Gombak.
Other affected areas include Gua Musang in Kelantan; Lipis and Cameron Highlands in Pahang; Jelebu, Kuala Pilah, Seremban and Rembau in Negeri Sembilan; and Alor Gajah in Melaka.
In Sarawak, the warning covers Selangau in Sibu; Tatau in Bintulu; Mukah, Pusa and Betong in Betong; Pantu and Lingga in Sri Aman; Kuching, Samarahan and Siburan in Serian; and Lawas in Limbang.
In Sabah, affected areas include Sipitang in the Interior Division; Kinabatangan and Paitan in Sandakan; and Ranau, Kota Belud and Tuaran in the West Coast Division. — Bernama

Title: Former Sungai Ujong undang to face sedition charge in Seremban tomorrow
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Former Sungai Ujong undang Datuk Mubarak Thahak @ Dohak is expected to face a sedition charge at the Seremban Sessions Court tomorrow over statements he allegedly made earlier this year.
Free Malaysia Today (FMT) reported that Mubarak would be charged before judge Tasnim Abu Bakar for allegedly uttering seditious statements.
The alleged offence took place on April 19, 2026, at the Balai Undang Luak Sungai Ujong in Seremban.
Mubarak was among four undangs at the centre of a constitutional crisis in Negeri Sembilan after they claimed that Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir had been removed as Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
Last month, the Dewan Keadilan dan Undang (DKU) gazetted Mubarak’s removal as Sungai Ujong undang, with the decision taking effect on May 13, 2025.
In September, former Senate president Rais Yatim was charged with sedition at the Melaka Sessions Court over the purported proclamation of a new Negeri Sembilan Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
Rais pleaded not guilty to the charge.
The full report is available here.

Title: MetMalaysia warns of continuous rain across Terengganu, parts of Kelantan until Sunday
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — The Malaysian Meteorological Department (MetMalaysia) has issued an alert-level warning for continuous rain in several areas in Kelantan and throughout Terengganu until Sunday (Nov 29).
MetMalaysia said in a statement that the warning in Kelantan covered Pasir Puteh, Bachok, Kota Bharu, Tumpat, Pasir Mas, Machang, Tanah Merah, Jeli and Kuala Krai.
An analysis of weather forecast models indicates that wind convergence is expected over the eastern part of the Peninsula until Sunday, potentially bringing continuous rain to both states throughout the period.
The public can get the latest weather updates through MetMalaysia’s official website, social media platforms and the myCuaca mobile application. — Bernama

Title: ‘Cooperating, not submitting’: Anwar defends PKR’s decision to sit out Sarawak polls
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has defended PKR’s decision not to contest the Sarawak state election, rejecting suggestions that the party was bowing to Gabungan Parti Sarawak (GPS) to preserve political ties at the federal level.
“I am cooperating, not submitting,” Anwar told reporters after launching the National Security Policy 2026-2030 today, Free Malaysia Today reported.
The PKR president and Pakatan Harapan (PH) chairman did not elaborate on the nature of the cooperation with GPS.
His remarks followed criticism from Sarawak DAP chairman Chong Chieng Jen, who accused PKR of “sacrificing democracy in Sarawak” to secure GPS’s continued support for the federal government.
DAP, which has announced 12 candidates so far, is the only PH component party contesting the election, with Amanah also opting out.
Earlier today, GPS information chief Datuk Seri Abdul Karim Rahman Hamzah defended the decisions of several national parties to stay out of the race, describing them as an exercise of their democratic rights.
He said the parties understood Sarawak’s political approach, which prioritised cooperation and stability, and argued that political competition at the state level should not undermine relationships at the federal level.
GPS, which governs Sarawak, is a key partner in Anwar’s federal administration.
In the 2021 election, GPS won 76 of the 82 state assembly seats, while DAP secured two. Neither PKR nor Amanah won any seats.
Polling is scheduled for December 12, with nominations on November 28 and early voting on December 8.

Title: No licence, no registration: Sabah wellness company fined RM30,000
Article:
KOTA KINABALU, Nov 26 — A company was fined RM30,000, in default six months’ imprisonment, by the Sessions Court here on Thursday for operating an unregistered private medical clinic.
Judge Marlina Ibrahim handed down the sentence to Katalina Aesthetic & Wellness Sdn Bhd after its director pleaded guilty on the company’s behalf to establishing Katalina Aesthetic & Wellness without registration under Section 27 of the Private Healthcare Facilities and Services Act 1998.
The offence was committed at Aeropod, off Jalan Kepayan, at about 11.40am on Oct 24, 2019, and carried a maximum fine of RM500,000 under Section 5(1)(b) of the same Act.
The court was informed that officers from the Sabah Health Department’s Private Medical Practice Control Section raided the premises on the said date, where staff failed to produce a clinic registration certificate or licence, and subsequently seized documents, medicines and machines. — Daily Express

Title: Zahid hints at end to Negeri Sembilan political crisis after royal audience, says palace to announce decision
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR، Nov 26 — The Negeri Sembilan Palace is expected to announce its decision on the positions of the menteri besar and state executive councillors following a meeting between the state’s Ruler and senior Barisan Nasional (BN) leaders this afternoon.
Deputy Prime Minister and BN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi indicated that an agreement had been reached during the audience، but said the final decision rested with Yang di-Pertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
Zahid، who is also Umno president، described the meeting as having taken place in a calm atmosphere،  Utusan Malaysia reported.
“We had an audience with Tuanku in a calm atmosphere، and Tuanku will make the decision.
“Let the statement from the palace finalise the decision that we have jointly agreed upon، ” he told reporters outside Istana Hinggap here today.
Zahid also indicated that the state’s political impasse could soon be resolved.
“God willing، it will be resolved soon، ” he said.
Zahid arrived at the palace at about 3pm and left approximately an hour later.
Also present were Umno deputy president and Negeri Sembilan BN chairman Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan، BN secretary-general Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir and Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Law and Institutional Reform) Datuk Seri Azalina Othman Said.
Earlier، Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim، who is also the Juasseh assemblyman، arrived at the palace at about 1.18pm for an audience with Tuanku Muhriz.
The meetings come amid continuing uncertainty over Ismail’s position and the functioning of the state administration.
The latest dispute arose on November 16 when Zambry announced Ismail’s purported resignation as menteri besar.
The following day، the palace clarified that Ismail remained in office، stating that under the state constitution، his resignation would only take effect upon its acceptance by the Yang di-Pertuan Besar.
On November 20، Ismail told reporters that he had neither submitted the resignation letter nor consented to its submission.
The palace also said Ismail was required to demonstrate that he retained majority support in the state legislative assembly and submit a proposed line-up of executive councillors for Tuanku Muhriz’s consideration.
Dates for the next state assembly sitting and the tabling of the 2027 state Budget would be determined once both matters had been resolved.
The state administration has been without its 10 executive councillors since their appointments were revoked by Tuanku Muhriz in September amid a dispute over the Ruler’s position.
It was previously reported that Ismail’s position was expected to be determined this week، following reports that all 24 BN and Perikatan Nasional (PN) assemblymen had lost confidence in his leadership.

Title: Malaysia keeps ex-prisoner reoffending rate at 11pc, among world’s best, says minister
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 26 — Malaysia recorded an average recidivism rate of 11 per cent among former prisoners nationwide this year, reflecting the effectiveness of rehabilitation programmes implemented by the Prisons Department.
Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said the rate was measured over a three-year period after an inmate’s release, placing Malaysia among the best-performing countries internationally.
“I am proud of this figure because we are among the best-performing countries, and I congratulate the Prisons Department on this achievement. However, I do not want them to become complacent.
“If possible, they should strive to bring the rate down to single digits,” he told reporters after attending the Home Ministry’s monthly assembly here today.
Saifuddin Nasution said the Prisons Department must continue improving its rehabilitation modules rather than rest on its achievements, to prevent former inmates from reoffending.
“These modules are not static. Through our engagement programmes with other countries, we identify good practices that may be suitable for adoption here.
“Each module is carefully designed to target rehabilitation in three aspects of human development: physical, spiritual and mental well-being. Its effectiveness is measured, among other things, through the recidivism rate,” he said.
Elaborating, Saifuddin said stigma and societal prejudice were among the factors that could drive former prisoners to reoffend, as they often struggled to gain acceptance after serving their sentences.
He said this was particularly challenging for former inmates convicted of drug-related offences, who often faced difficulties securing support from their families and communities, hindering their reintegration into society.
He urged the public to discard prejudices against former prisoners and allow them to rebuild their lives.
To support their reintegration, the Prisons Department has also established 13 halfway houses for former inmates who lack family or community support, including those who have secured employment but have nowhere to live.
Saifuddin Nasution added that about 75 per cent of the country’s prison population comprised individuals convicted of drug-related offences. — Bernama

Title: Amir Hamzah says domestic air links remain priority, but no AirAsia bailout promised
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Domestic air connectivity remains a government priority, while AirAsia Group Bhd’s financial position continues to be monitored to ensure the country’s aviation ecosystem is not disrupted, Finance Minister II Datuk Seri Amir Hamzah Azizan said.
He stressed that the government had made no agreement or commitment to provide financial support to AirAsia, whether through loan guarantees or injections of public funds.
“Air connectivity, particularly to Sabah and Sarawak, remains a government priority, given the reliance of a significant proportion of air services in both states on AirAsia,” he said during a Special Chamber session in the Dewan Rakyat today.
Amir Hamzah was responding to concerns over AirAsia’s financial position and the possibility of government intervention raised by Datuk Muhammad Bakhtiar Wan Chik (PKR-Balik Pulau).
He said the government was seeking views from various stakeholders, including industry players and technical experts, to better understand the challenges facing the airline and identify possible approaches.
“If the company’s financial position continues to deteriorate and the government needs to consider other options in the future, any approach will prioritise the interests of the people and ensure the continuity of domestic air services,” he said.
Amir Hamzah added that any application for government support from companies in any sector would be assessed based on national and public interests, the government’s fiscal sustainability and the protection of public funds, in accordance with prevailing laws and procedures.
He said the government aimed to ensure a sustainable aviation industry structure, rational competition and financially sound airlines, without reliance on related companies or the need for future government intervention.
On AirAsia’s financial difficulties, he said the challenges were not new but dated back to the Covid-19 pandemic, when the airline faced financial constraints and various difficulties following its restructuring under PN17 status.
The situation had become more challenging following the West Asia crisis, which had driven aviation fuel prices to more than US$200 a barrel from about US$90 previously.
“Other airlines have also recorded losses under such circumstances,” he said.
AirAsia Group accounted for about 45 per cent of the 104.5 million passenger movements recorded at airports operated by Malaysia Airports Holdings Bhd in 2025, as well as nearly 60 per cent of domestic passenger movements, he said.
In 2026, AirAsia carried 62 per cent of passengers in Sabah and 70 per cent in Sarawak, based on the latest available data.
The airports with the highest AirAsia passenger shares included Sandakan (80 per cent), Sibu (76 per cent), Bintulu and Tawau (74 per cent each), Kuching (69 per cent), Miri (66 per cent) and Kota Kinabalu (61 per cent).
In Peninsular Malaysia, AirAsia also accounted for significant passenger shares in Johor (70 per cent), Terengganu (56 per cent), Langkawi (56 per cent), Alor Setar (49 per cent), Kelantan (46 per cent) and Penang (36 per cent).
At KLIA Terminal 2 (KLIA2), AirAsia Group accounted for 88 per cent of total passenger movements.
Responding to a supplementary question from Muhammad Bakhtiar on whether the government’s proposed approach would mirror its handling of Sapura Energy Bhd, now known as Vantris Energy Bhd, Amir Hamzah said one key consideration was to strengthen the company’s board and management while resolving its problems to build a more sustainable entity.
He said that if the government had to intervene in AirAsia’s case, it would adopt an approach similar to that used for Vantris.
“We must ensure that, in providing any assistance, the government receives priority over those who have already lent money to AirAsia.
“We want to ensure that public funds receive the priority they deserve, as the government would be stepping in as a rescuer in such circumstances.
“Our aim is not to protect shareholders, but to protect the people,” he said.
Amir Hamzah also said the AirAsia Group structure was complex, as it owned several airlines, each holding its own Air Operator Certificate in Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, the Philippines and Cambodia.
Capital A Bhd, meanwhile, is a separate listed company that provides essential services to AirAsia, including catering, aircraft maintenance and cargo services. — Bernama

Title: Sacked ‘Inspector Sheila’ gets court nod to challenge dismissal, seeks reinstatement and back pay
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Former police inspector SK Sheila Sharon has secured permission from the High Court to challenge her dismissal from the force as she seeks reinstatement, back pay and damages.
The 38-year-old was granted leave to commence judicial review proceedings today, Harian Metro reported.
High Court judge S Indra Nehru granted the application after Federal Counsel Mohd Solihin Md Zaki raised no objection.
A date for the substantive hearing has yet to be fixed.
Sheila filed her application on October 29 through law firm M Manoharan & Co, naming former Deputy Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Ayob Khan Mydin Pitchay, the police disciplinary board, the Police Force Commission and the Malaysian government as respondents.
According to her supporting affidavit, Sheila claimed she had received a dismissal letter dated July 7 this year from Ayob Khan, who was then chairman of the disciplinary board, in connection with 23 disciplinary offences within the force.
She is seeking a court declaration that the decision to dismiss her, conveyed through two disciplinary punishment notification letters dated July 7 and received on August 3, was invalid and unlawful.
Sheila wants the court to quash the disciplinary decision and order her reinstatement to the police force with her rank of inspector intact.
She is also seeking payment of outstanding salaries, allowances, bonuses and other employment entitlements from July 3, which she cited as the date of her dismissal, until her reinstatement.
Her application further seeks to have all entries relating to the disciplinary decision and punishment removed from her service record.
Sheila is also claiming general, aggravated and exemplary damages, with the amount to be determined by the court, as well as interest at five per cent per annum from the date of judgment until full settlement, costs and other appropriate relief.
The granting of leave allows Sheila to proceed with her legal challenge but does not constitute a ruling on the lawfulness of her dismissal.

Title: Anwar says Putrajaya cuts new borrowing to RM70b, but legacy debts linger
Article:
KUALA TERENGGANU, Nov 26 — The government has reduced its annual new borrowings from about RM100 billion when it took over the administration of the country to about RM70 billion currently, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said.
He said the reduction had been achieved gradually.
However, he said the government still had to service and repay legacy debts inherited from previous administrations, including those involving 1Malaysia Development Berhad (1MDB), the Federal Land Development Authority (Felda) and Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH).
“Those old debts still carry interest that has to be paid. The debts involving 1MDB, Tabung Haji and Felda still have to be settled to this day.
“I have only reduced new borrowing, but the old debts still have to be repaid, which is why the country’s total debt still appears high,” he said.
He was speaking at the launch of the Terengganu Skim Usahawan Bangkit programme organised by the Prime Minister’s Department Implementation Coordination Unit (ICU JPM) here today.
He said the government had to continue meeting these debt obligations to safeguard the country’s financial position and ensure the continued operations of the institutions concerned.
Anwar said the government had to pay nearly RM1 billion annually to settle Felda’s legacy debts, including about RM980 million.
He said similar responsibilities involving TH had to be met to safeguard depositors’ funds and the welfare of haj pilgrims.
“Prudent management of the country’s finances is important to ensure the government can meet its existing commitments without compromising its ability to provide assistance and facilities to the people,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Johor sets aside RM20.73m to reduce flood risks in 2027
Article:
ISKANDAR PUTERI, Nov 26 — The Johor state government has allocated RM20.73 million through the Department of Irrigation and Drainage (DID) for initiatives aimed at reducing flood risks next year, said state Public Works, Transport, Infrastructure and Communications Committee chairman Mohamad Fazli Mohamad Salleh.
He said the allocation covers several initiatives, including 12 studies valued at RM1.54 million, seven flood mitigation projects (RM1.61 million) and three drainage projects (RM1.2 million).
“The allocation also covers four coastal zone projects (RM2.7 million), 14 river basin projects (RM5.58 million), 12 agricultural drainage projects (RM3.08 million), eight river estuary projects (RM2.52 million), as well as minor related works valued at RM2.5 million,” he said during the winding-up session of the Johor Budget 2027 debate at the state legislative assembly in Kota Iskandar today.
Mohamad Fazli also said the Johor DID had been allocated RM43.6 million for development, covering 112 initiatives across two main pillars to strengthen the management of irrigation, drainage and flood mitigation infrastructure.
He noted that Johor has 20 major river basins, while its drainage network extends over 5,853km and requires periodic maintenance, at an estimated cost of RM92 million this year.
On water supply infrastructure, including dams and rivers, Mohamad Fazli said RM640,000 had been allocated for the construction of five telemetry stations in Kluang, Pontian, Tangkak and Johor Bahru (RM500,000), and the upgrading of two water-level gauges in Pontian and Johor Bahru (RM140,000).
The Bukit Pasir assemblyman added that RM800,000 had been set aside for agricultural road projects at two locations: Lubuk Kepong in Gemas, Segamat (RM500,000), and Kampung Melayu Nyior in Kluang (RM300,000).
“Additionally, RM30 million, sourced from the Malaysian Road Records Information System (MARRIS) allocation, has been channelled to the DID for the maintenance of agricultural roads,” he said.
Under the Johor Budget 2027, RM1.19 billion was allocated for 33 initiatives under the public works, transport, infrastructure and communications portfolio, representing approximately 38.8 per cent of the state’s total projected expenditure.

Title: All eyes on Istana Hinggap as Zahid, Tok Mat meet Negeri Sembilan Ruler
Article:
SEREMBAN, Nov 26 — Umno president Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi and deputy president Datuk Seri Mohamad Hasan arrived at Istana Hinggap here at 3pm for an audience with the Yang di-Pertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir.
Earlier, Tuanku Muhriz arrived at the palace at about 1.30pm.
Also present was Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim, who arrived at the palace at 1.18pm.
It is understood that the meeting is aimed at resolving the state’s political crisis, particularly concerning the position of the menteri besar.
Negeri Sembilan’s political crisis erupted on November 16 when Barisan Nasional (BN) secretary-general Datuk Seri Zambry Abd Kadir announced that Ismail had resigned as menteri besar.
Zambry said Ahmad Zahid, who is also BN chairman, had received a copy of the resignation letter and would submit a proposed candidate to succeed Ismail to Tuanku Muhriz.
However, the Negeri Sembilan Palace said on November 17 that the menteri besar’s resignation would take effect only upon receiving Tuanku Muhriz’s consent.
On November 20, Ismail said he had neither submitted the resignation letter nor consented to its submission to Tuanku Muhriz.
The palace subsequently clarified that Ismail needed to demonstrate that he still commanded the support of a majority of state assembly members to determine his position as menteri besar.
The development followed reports that 24 BN and Perikatan Nasional (PN) assemblymen had agreed to abide by the decisions of their respective party leaderships on resolving the state’s political crisis.
Ismail, who is also the Juasseh assemblyman, was sworn in as Negeri Sembilan menteri besar on August 2.
In the 16th Negeri Sembilan state election, BN won 18 seats while PN secured seven of the 36 seats in the state legislative assembly. — Bernama

Title: Home minister says police must apply law equally to both sides of political divide
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 26 — Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said police must investigate all reports regardless of political affiliation, following questions about the investigation involving former DAP MP Tony Pua over the alleged disclosure of Pardons Board meeting minutes concerning former prime minister Datuk Seri Najib Razak.
He said police must discharge their responsibilities without restrictions or favouritism to dispel perceptions that the authorities were more lenient towards government supporters.
“Police often face accusations of conducting selective investigations, while the Attorney General is accused of selective prosecution.
“The reality is that when a statement is made and a police report is lodged, the police open an investigation. I leave that to the professionalism of the police force,” Utusan Malaysia quoted him as saying after the Home Ministry’s monthly assembly here today.
Saifuddin was responding to questions about the progress of the investigation involving Pua, who shared purported excerpts from the Pardons Board meeting minutes on social media.
The home minister also called for consistency in how political parties responded to police investigations, saying the principle of fairness should apply to everyone.
“It doesn’t matter who it is. Anyone. We have no restrictions whatsoever,” he said.
He added that those who criticised police for allegedly taking swift action against opposition figures should not object when government supporters faced similar scrutiny.
“Be fair to everyone,” he said.
On Tuesday, Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail said police had not ruled out calling Pua to assist in the investigation into the alleged disclosure.
The controversy concerns minutes of the Pardons Board meeting relating to Najib’s reduced prison sentence and the purported royal addendum concerning house arrest.
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim told the Dewan Rakyat on Tuesday that the government had not publicly released the minutes, explaining that portions of the document had been declassified for use in related court proceedings.

Title: Johor launches MyJT transport app to help commuters track buses, plan journeys
Article:
JOHOR BAHRU, Nov 26 — The newly introduced MyJohor Transport (MyJT) application aims to make public transport more reliable and convenient for commuters in the city, particularly bus passengers.
Developed by Pengangkutan Awam Johor (PAJ), the app allows users to locate their nearest bus stops and check estimated bus arrival times.
Johor Public Works, Transport, Infrastructure and Communications Committee chairman Mohamad Fazli Mohamad Salleh said a key feature of the application allows passengers using the Bas Muafakat Johor service to plan their journeys more accurately.
“Users no longer need to wait for long periods without knowing what to expect. By checking the latest route schedules and the locations of nearby stops, their daily travel becomes much more convenient,” he told reporters after attending a Bas Muafakat Johor event at the Opero Hotel here yesterday, which also saw the launch of the MyJT app and the Bus On Demand service.
Also present were PAJ chief executive officer Mohd Faiz Salehon and members of its senior management.
Mohamad Fazli said information on existing bus stops would also be digitised to improve access to travel information, adding that the initiative could help ease traffic congestion.
He said visitors from Singapore could also use the bus service by purchasing a 14-day tourist pass for RM30.
“Through this application, we can maintain records of Bas Muafakat Johor’s usage, which in turn supports the expansion of the bus fleet in operation.
“The use of the application does not cause confusion with existing systems, such as MyBorderPass, and can be integrated with related systems,” he said.

Title: Terengganu’s ECRL races towards Dec 12 launch as project hits 99.5pc completion
Article:
MARANG, Nov 26 — The construction of the East Coast Rail Link (ECRL) project in Terengganu is nearing completion, with progress reaching an encouraging 99.54 per cent ahead of the commencement of commercial operations on Dec 12.
Chief Secretary to the Government Tan Sri Shamsul Azri Abu Bakar, also the Malaysia Rail Link Sdn Bhd (MRL) chairman, said the 242-kilometre (km) ECRL alignment in Terengganu comprises six stations, which will serve as new transportation hubs in the state.
He said the Jerteh, Bandar Permaisuri, Kuala Terengganu and Kemasik stations would cater exclusively to passenger services, while the Dungun and Chukai stations would serve both passenger and cargo services.
“Construction progress for the first phase of the ECRL project reached 99.03 per cent as of October and is ready to connect the state with other destinations along the East Coast and in the Klang Valley,” he said in his speech at the opening ceremony of the Kuala Terengganu ECRL Station in Durian Guling near here today.
The station was officially opened by the Regent of Terengganu, Tengku Muhammad Ismail Sultan Mizan Zainal Abidin.
Also present were the Menteri Besar of Terengganu, Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Samsuri Mokhtar, and MRL chief executive officer Datuk Seri Darwis Abdul Razak.
At the ceremony, Tengku Muhammad Ismail took a ride on the ECRL train from the Kuala Terengganu Station to the Dungun Station to experience first-hand its fast, safe and comfortable journey.
In a related development, Shamsul Azri said the ECRL is currently undergoing a trial run from Nov 7 to Dec 2 in preparation for the commencement of commercial services.
He said preparations also included comprehensive training for the local workforce, including Terengganu-born personnel, to ensure the highest standards of operational efficiency and passenger safety.
“The ECRL train ride from Kuala Terengganu to Kota Bharu (Kelantan) is expected to take around one hour, while the journey to Gombak is only around three hours,” he added.
In another development, he said the Kuala Terengganu ECRL station is also equipped with various modern facilities, including VIP and business-class lounges, passenger waiting areas, escalators, convenience stores, 500 parking bays, covered pedestrian walkways and well-planned landscaping.
“The presence of this station and modern rail services will not only further boost Terengganu’s tourism sector but also create more economic and trade opportunities, while providing convenient mobility for the people of Terengganu,” he added.
He said the Kuala Terengganu ECRL station, built on a 24.99-hectare site, features an architectural design inspired by boats and waves, reflecting Terengganu’s maritime identity.
“This concept highlights the unique heritage of traditional wooden boat craftsmanship, which is a source of pride for the people of Terengganu, while combining modern infrastructure with the richness of the state’s heritage,” he said. — Bernama

Title: Muhyiddin ‘chose to close his eyes’ over RM25.3m in Bersatu accounts, prosecution says
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — Former prime minister Tan Sri Muhyiddin Yassin had intentionally closed his eyes on the source of the RM25.3 million which had entered his party Parti Pribumi Bersatu Malaysia’s two bank accounts in 2021 and 2022, the prosecution said at the High Court today.
At Muhyiddin’s power abuse trial today, the prosecution argued that the RM25.3 million was not a “bona fide” donation to Bersatu, but were instead rewards given after three Bumiputera contractors received government projects under the Jana Wibawa programme.
Lead prosecutor Datuk Wan Shaharuddin Wan Ladin said Muhyiddin’s trial is the first-ever case in Malaysia involving a prime minister’s alleged power abuse for the financial benefit of its “associate”, Bersatu.
He said this is unlike past corruption cases involving alleged power abuse for a public body officer’s own interest (such as 1MDB, SRC International) or for their relative’s interest.
Wan Shaharuddin said that Bersatu would not have received RM25.3 million if Muhyiddin was not both the prime minister and Bersatu president at the same time, and if he had not opened the way for the Bumiputera contractors to be considered for the projects.
“When the accused took action to help facilitate, paving the way for KCJ, Nepturis, Sutracom to enter the evaluation process by the Jana Wibawa evaluation committee, it has paved the way, that cannot be denied,” he said, referring to the three companies which had either directly or via affiliates paid the RM25.3 million.
While acknowledging that Muhyiddin did not have the power to ensure that those three Bumiputera firms would win the projects, Wan Shaharuddin emphasised the politician’s role in facilitating their inclusion in the Finance Ministry’s evaluation process for Jana Wibawa projects.
“And the end result in this case, they really did get those projects. And the end result from that, the ripple effect, because of that — they received the project, they put the money into Bersatu,” he said.
Disputing Muhyiddin’s defence that the RM25.3 million is a “political donation”, Wan Shaharuddin said it is “glaring” that the money is not a “bona fide” donation, as those linked to the contractors have testified in court that “this is a ‘balasan’, reward.”
Among other things, Wan Shaharuddin argued that the three individuals who testified on the RM25.3 million that their companies had given to Bersatu are credible witnesses.
These three are Mamfor Sdn Bhd’s managing director Shahradzi Shamsuddin (who gave the money after his younger brother’s company Sutracom obtained a Jana Wibawa project), Nepturis Sdn Bhd’s hidden shareholder Lian Tan Chuan, and KCJ Engineering Sdn Bhd’s managing director Datuk Seri Azman Yusoff.
Why prosecution says Muhyiddin was wilfully blindWan Shaharuddin today referred to the Tropicana Golf Club incident in July 2020, where there was a private meeting between Muhyiddin and KCJ’s Azman (who was also the Bumiputera Contractors Association of Malaysia (PKBM) president).
Azman previously testified that he had asked Muhyiddin about opportunities for government projects for PKBM members, and that Muhyiddin had then told him about the Jana Wibawa programme and also “spontaneously” said contractors who wished to donate could donate directly to Bersatu.
Wan Shaharuddin questioned the need for Muhyiddin to speak about donations to Bersatu in that meeting and how it was related to the issue of helping Bumiputera contractors with opportunities for projects, saying: “That conversation does not gel.”
“What happened at Tropicana when he mentioned ‘sumbangan’ (contribution / donation) to Bersatu is an action that creates a conflict of interest. He is the prime minister to all Malaysians and the interest is to Bersatu,” he said, arguing that Muhyiddin had been thinking of his associate Bersatu’s interests then.
When the funds totalling RM25.3 million later came into Bersatu’s accounts in CIMB and AmBank, Wan Shaharuddin said Muhyiddin has the responsibility to know the money’s source as he was Bersatu president and the accounts’ trustee and authorised signatory.
He argued that Muhyiddin intentionally failed to check the source of the RM25.3 million.
“He is not an ordinary member, he is a trustee to the CIMB and AmBank accounts. He should know about the RM25.3 million, but he chose to close his eyes. It is not RM100, but RM25.3 million,” he said.
He argued that a “prudent” and “vigilant” man would have checked with the bank, and taken steps such as returning the money if he had discovered that it was from KCJ’s Azman who he had played golf with.
At one point, Wan Shaharuddin described Muhyiddin as having shown “wilful blindness” about the RM25.3 million: “He chose to shut the eyes to what is obvious.”
Ultimately, Wan Shaharuddin argued that the prosecution has successfully proven a prima facie case against Muhyiddin on all three power abuse charges against him under Section 23(1) of the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission Act 2009.
In criminal trials, the prosecution has to prove a prima facie case, or to show there is a case for an accused person to answer by entering their defence.
The trial before High Court judge Noor Ruwena Md Nurdin will resume on December 1, where Muhyiddin’s lawyers are expected to present arguments on why he should not be called to enter defence.

Title: Malaysia’s gender gap narrows in the workplace, but women still underrepresented in politics
Article:
PUTRAJAYA, Nov 26 — Malaysia’s gender gap narrowed slightly in 2025 as the Malaysia Gender Gap Index (MGGI) rose to 0.711 from 0.708 in 2024.
The Department of Statistics Malaysia (DOSM) said the improvement was mainly driven by better economic participation and opportunity, with the subindex rising to 0.728 from 0.703.
DOSM said women’s labour force participation rate rose slightly to 56.6 per cent in 2025 from 56.5 per cent in 2024, while their mean monthly salaries and wages increased to RM3,635 from RM3,499.
The number of women working as legislators, senior officials and managers increased to 241,000 from 219,000. Those in professional and technical occupations rose to 1.8 million from 1.7 million.
“The MGGI measures the gender gap between women and men in four areas, namely economic participation and opportunity, educational attainment, health and survival, and political empowerment,” DOSM said in its MGGI 2026 report released today.
A score of 1.000 indicates full equality between women and men, the department said.
It said the educational attainment subindex stood at 1.064 in 2025, compared with 1.073 in 2024.
“Female students recorded higher gross enrolment rates at the secondary and tertiary levels, at 95.9 per cent and 57.1 per cent respectively, while the rate for both males and females at the primary level was 99.7 per cent,” it said, adding that the health and survival subindex stood at 0.957 in 2025, with women’s life expectancy at birth rising to 77.8 years from 65.6 years in 1970.
However, political empowerment remained the weakest area, with a score of just 0.094.
DOSM said women accounted for only 15.6 per cent of ministerial positions and 13.5 per cent of seats in the Dewan Rakyat.
“This reflects the continuing challenges in achieving gender balance in political leadership and decision-making in Malaysia,” it said, adding that at the state level, Kuala Lumpur recorded the highest MGGI score at 0.781, followed by Labuan at 0.756 and Putrajaya at 0.754.
Five states recorded scores below the national level of 0.711, namely Melaka (0.707), Terengganu (0.706), Pahang (0.704), Sarawak (0.698) and Johor (0.693). — Bernama

Title: Woman survives apparent fall from 21st floor of KL flats, in stable condition
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 26 — A 29-year-old woman has survived an apparent fall from the 21st floor of a block of flats in Kuala Lumpur and is reported to be in stable condition in hospital.
The incident involving the Indian national occurred this morning, Utusan Malaysia reported.
Brickfields district police chief Assistant Commissioner Hoo Chang Hook said police were alerted at about 11.02am.
He said officers found several of the woman’s personal belongings on the floor from which she was believed to have fallen.
“The victim was taken to Kuala Lumpur Hospital (HKL) for treatment and is currently in the emergency ward.
“She is reported to be in stable condition but sustained fractures to her left leg and right arm,” he said in a statement today.
Police investigations found that the woman was not a resident of the flats and was believed to be from Segambut.
The circumstances surrounding the incident remain unclear, with police yet to record statements from any witnesses.
“Police are also working to locate the victim’s next of kin to assist in the investigation,” Hoo added.
